definition_zh: 银杏树；银杏果；白果
definition_en: a tall tree with fan-shaped leaves, native to China, or its edible seed
core_image: 一把张开的绿扇子：扇形叶片长在古老的枝头
scene: 深秋的公园里，一棵老树的叶子像小扇子一样铺满地面。Every autumn the old ginkgo drops its fan-shaped leaves across the park path.
sceneCN: 这里 ginkgo 是「银杏树」（第 1 个义项：长着扇形叶的古老乔木）；句意：每到秋天，这棵老银杏就把扇形的叶子落满公园的小路。

derivatives.zh: 银杏科的（由 ginkgo 加形容词后缀 -aceous 构成）
银杏科（拉丁科名，由属名 Ginkgo 加科名后缀 -aceae 构成）

senses.title: The tree with fan-shaped leaves
senses.definition: a tall deciduous tree with fan-shaped leaves, the only living species of its order
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大的落叶乔木，叶子呈扇形，是其所属目现存的唯一物种
senses.example: A ginkgo can live for more than a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵银杏可以活一千年以上。
senses.why: The name entered English as a tree name first, so the plant itself is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字最初就是以树名进入英语的，所以树本身是最核心的义项。

senses.title: The edible seed
senses.definition: the seed of the tree, often roasted and eaten in Chinese cooking
senses.definitionCN: 这种树的种子，在中餐里常炒熟食用
senses.example: Roasted ginkgo seeds are sold in small paper bags in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天，炒熟的银杏果装在小纸袋里出售。
senses.why: People gather the seed rather than the wood, so the tree name passed to the nut.
senses.whyCN: 人们采集的是种子而不是木材，所以树名自然转指果实。

senses.title: A leaf-based herbal supplement
senses.definition: an extract of the leaves sold as a dietary supplement
senses.definitionCN: 用叶子提取、作为膳食补充剂出售的产品
senses.example: Some people take ginkgo to help their memory.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人服用银杏制剂来帮助记忆。
senses.why: Modern marketing stretched the plant name to the bottled extract on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 现代营销把植物名延伸到了货架上的瓶装提取物。

senses.title: A living fossil lineage
senses.definition: the ancient group of trees that survived almost unchanged for millions of years
senses.definitionCN: 历经数百万年几乎未曾改变的古老树木类群
senses.example: Botanists call the ginkgo a living fossil.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把银杏称作活化石。
senses.why: The tree is the last survivor of a huge ancient group, so its name also labels that lineage.
senses.whyCN: 这种树是一个庞大古老类群的最后幸存者，所以名字也指这一世系。

intro.en: Ginkgo reached European science through Japan: the Chinese tree name was borrowed into Japanese and then Latinized in 1690.
intro.cn: ginkgo 经日本进入欧洲科学：汉语的树名先被日语借去，1690 年再被拉丁化。

items.en: The tree is called yinxing, literally silver apricot.
items.cn: 这种树在汉语里叫「银杏」，字面意思是银白色的杏。

items.en: Japanese borrowed the name and pronounced it ginkyo for the tree and its nut.
items.cn: 日语借用了这个名字，读作 ginkyo，既指树也指它的果实。

items.en: Engelbert Kaempfer published the Latinized form Ginkgo.
items.cn: 坎普弗发表了拉丁化写法 Ginkgo。

items.en: Linnaeus used Ginkgo as a genus name in his later botanical work.
items.cn: 林奈在后期植物学著作中把 Ginkgo 用作属名。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin name and kept the unusual g spelling.
items.cn: 英语借用这个拉丁名，并保留了那个不寻常的 g 拼法。

note.en: Ginkgo is a one-species genus, so its nearest words are the Latin genus and family names plus the older English tree names.
note.cn: ginkgo 是只有一个物种的属，与它最近的是拉丁属名、科名，以及英语里更早的树名。

entries.definition: belonging to the ginkgo family
the botanical family that contains the ginkgo
entries.definitionCN: 银杏科，含银杏的植物科

entries.definition: the species epithet meaning two-lobed
entries.definitionCN: 种加词，意为「两裂的」，指裂开的叶形

entries.definition: the older English common name for the ginkgo
entries.definitionCN: 银杏的旧英文俗名，因叶形似少女的发丝

entries.definition: a similar ancient seed plant with palm-like leaves
entries.definitionCN: 苏铁，一类外观相近的古老裸子植物

entries.definition: a plant whose seeds are not enclosed in a fruit
entries.definitionCN: 种子不被果实包住的植物，即裸子植物

normalIntro.en: Ginkgo is a borrowed tree name, so its hooks come from the fan leaf, the seed, and the Chinese origin.
normalIntro.cn: ginkgo 是一个借来的树名，记忆钩子来自扇形叶、种子与汉语来源。

normal.en: The fan-shaped leaf is the quickest way to recognise a ginkgo.
normal.cn: 扇形叶是认出银杏最快的办法。

normal.en: Ginkgo biloba is the full botanical name printed on supplement bottles.
normal.cn: 银杏瓶子上印的完整学名是「Ginkgo biloba」。

normal.en: A ginkgo nut is called baiguo in Chinese and is eaten roasted.
normal.cn: 银杏果在中文里叫「白果」，常炒熟吃。

normal.en: The word came through Japanese, which is why the spelling looks unlike other tree names.
normal.cn: 这个词经日语传来，所以拼法与别的树名都不一样。

normal.en: Remember the double consonant look: ginkgo keeps the Latinized spelling, not ginkyo.
normal.cn: 记住那个双写的拼法：写作 ginkgo，而不是 ginkyo。

abstract.en: See a green fan opening on an ancient branch.
abstract.cn: 想象古老的枝头张开一把绿扇。

abstract.en: Picture a small paper bag of warm roasted seeds.
abstract.cn: 想象一小纸袋热腾腾的炒种子。

abstract.en: Think of a brown bottle standing on a pharmacy shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象药房货架上立着一只棕色瓶子。

examples.en: The ginkgo in our courtyard turns gold in November.
examples.cn: 我们院子里的银杏在十一月变成金黄色。

examples.en: She planted a row of ginkgos along the driveway.
examples.cn: 她沿车道种了一排银杏。

examples.en: Ginkgo leaves are shaped like small fans.
examples.cn: 银杏叶的形状像小扇子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「根够」——银杏的根扎得够深，扇形叶才站得稳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自汉语「银杏」的日语读法 ginkyo，1690 年由坎普弗拉丁化为 Ginkgo，1771 年林奈用作属名；词中 g 的来历存疑，多认为是误读，属于首见拼写问题而非词源问题。

sensesIntro.en: Ginkgo names the tree first, then its seed, then the leaf extract sold as a supplement, and finally the ancient lineage the tree represents.
sensesIntro.cn: ginkgo 先指树，再指它的种子，再指作为保健品出售的叶提取物，最后指这棵树所代表的古老世系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green fan leaf on an ancient tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：古老树木上的一片绿扇叶。

branches.en: The tree itself is the original sense.
branches.cn: 树本身是最初的义项。

branches.en: The seed people eat takes the same name.
branches.cn: 人们食用的种子沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: The bottled leaf extract is a modern extension.
branches.cn: 瓶装叶提取物是现代引申。

branches.en: The lineage sense grows from the tree being a lone survivor.
branches.cn: 世系义项来自这棵树是孤独幸存者这一事实。

branches.en: The tree and its lineage are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 树与它的世系由同一个词来命名。

intro.en: Ginkgo is a Latinized Japanese form of a Chinese tree name; its word family is botanical rather than everyday.
intro.cn: ginkgo 是汉语树名经日语再拉丁化的形式；它的词族偏植物学，而不是日常词汇。

latinIntro.en: The genus name Ginkgo was fixed by Linnaeus, and the family name adds the botanical suffix -aceae.
latinIntro.cn: 属名 Ginkgo 由林奈确定，科名则加上植物学的科名后缀 -aceae。

items.example: Ginkgo is both the tree and the nut.
items.exampleCN: ginkgo 既指树也指果。

items.example: Ginkgo is the genus name on the label.
items.exampleCN: Ginkgo 是标签上的属名。

items.example: Japanese ginkyo is the source of the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 日语的 ginkyo 是拉丁写法的来源。

items.meaningCN: 银杏；字面义银白色的杏
items.example: Yinxing is the Chinese name behind the Japanese form.
items.exampleCN: yinxing 是日语写法背后的汉语名称。

items.meaningCN: 植物学中表示科名的后缀
items.example: The suffix -aceae builds Ginkgoaceae.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aceae 构成 Ginkgoaceae。

items.example: Ginkgoaceae contains only one living genus.
items.exampleCN: 银杏科只有一个现存属。

items.example: The suffix -aceous builds ginkgoaceous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aceous 构成 ginkgoaceous。

items.example: Ginkgoaceous leaves appear in the fossil record.
items.exampleCN: 化石记录里出现了银杏科的叶子。

items.example: Biloba describes the split leaf of the species.
items.exampleCN: biloba 描述这个物种裂开的叶子。

definition_zh: 腰带；环带；环绕；环剥
definition_en: a belt worn around the waist, or to encircle something
core_image: 一条束在腰上的带子，把身体围成一圈
scene: 旧时的人把皮制带子束在腰间，走起路来叮当作响。The old blacksmith wore a leather girdle around his waist as he worked.
sceneCN: 这里 girdle 是「腰带」（第 1 个义项：束在腰间的带子）；句意：那位老铁匠干活时腰间系着一条皮带。

derivatives.zh: 束（腰带）；围绕（与 girdle 同出的古英语动词）
解开腰带（gird 加否定前缀 un- 构成）
环剥；环割（girdle 加 -ing 构成的名词）

senses.title: A belt worn around the waist
senses.definition: a band or belt that fastens around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 束在腰间、用来系紧衣服的带子
senses.example: A leather girdle held his tunic tight.
senses.exampleCN: 一条皮腰带把他的长袍束紧。
senses.why: Old English gyrdel simply names the thing that girds the waist.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gyrdel 直接指「把腰束住」的那件东西。

senses.title: An elastic undergarment for the lower body
senses.definition: a close-fitting elastic garment worn around the waist and hips
senses.definitionCN: 紧贴腰胯、有弹性的内衣
senses.example: The dress of that era needed a firm girdle beneath it.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年代的裙子下面需要一件紧实的束身内衣。
senses.why: Because a girdle grips the body, the same word came to name a shaping garment.
senses.whyCN: 因为腰带紧勒身体，同一个词又用来指塑形的内衣。

senses.title: Something that encircles
senses.definition: a ring or band of something that surrounds a place or object
senses.definitionCN: 环绕某个地方或物体的一圈东西
senses.example: A girdle of pines circled the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 一圈松树围着那座老房子。
senses.why: The belt image moved outward: anything drawn around a thing forms a girdle.
senses.whyCN: 腰带意象向外扩展：凡是绕着某物围成一圈的东西都成了 girdle。

senses.title: To surround or encircle
senses.definition: to go around something so as to enclose it
senses.definitionCN: 绕在四周，把某物围在中间
senses.example: Rivers girdle the old city on three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 河水从三面环绕这座古城。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of the same shape: to put a girdle around.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转为同形的动词：给某物围上这么一圈。

senses.title: To cut a ring of bark from a tree
senses.definition: to remove a band of bark around a trunk, often to check or kill a tree
senses.definitionCN: 在树干上剥去一圈树皮，常用于控制生长或使树枯死
senses.example: Farmers girdle a tree to stop it from fruiting.
senses.exampleCN: 农民会环剥树干，让树不再结果。
senses.why: The ring of a belt gave foresters a word for a ring cut into bark.
senses.whyCN: 腰带的一圈，让林业工作者用同一个词指刻在树皮上的一圈切口。

intro.en: Girdle goes back to Old English gyrdel, a belt, from the verb gird, and is related to girth.
intro.cn: girdle 可追溯到古英语 gyrdel（腰带），源自动词 gird，并与 girth 同源。

items.en: A root meaning to grasp or enclose lies behind the whole family.
items.cn: 一个意为「抓住、围住」的词根是这整个词族的来源。

items.en: Gurdlaz names a belt or girdle.
items.cn: gurdlaz 指腰带或束带。

items.en: Gyrdel appears as the everyday word for a belt.
items.cn: gyrdel 作为腰带的日常说法出现。

items.en: Girdel keeps the belt sense and gains the shaping garment sense.
items.cn: girdel 保留腰带义，并增加塑形内衣义。

items.en: Modern English adds the ring sense, the verb, and the forestry term.
items.cn: 现代英语增加环带义、动词用法与林业术语义。

note.en: Girdle sits in a small family of waist and ring words, and its near meanings are belts and encircling garments.
note.cn: girdle 属于一个由「腰」与「圈」组成的小词族，近义词是腰带与围身衣物。

entries.definition: to fasten with a belt
to encircle, in older use
the distance around a body
a band worn around the waist
a long strip of cloth worn around the waist
a stiff shaping garment for the waist
entries.definitionCN: 紧勒腰部、起塑形作用的硬质内衣

normalIntro.en: Girdle is a waist word first, so its family and collocations come from belts, rings, and trees.
normalIntro.cn: girdle 首先是「腰」的词，它的词族与搭配来自腰带、圈和树。

normal.en: Girdle and gird share the same old verb; a girdle is what girds you.
normal.cn: girdle 与 gird 同出一个古老动词：girdle 就是把腰束住的东西。

normal.en: Girth and girdle both measure a circle around a body.
normal.cn: girth 与 girdle 都表示身体外面的一圈。

normal.en: A pelvic girdle is the bony ring at the hips, not a cloth belt.
normal.cn: 骨盆带是髋部的骨环，不是布腰带。

normal.en: To girdle a tree is to cut a ring of bark, a forestry use of the belt image.
normal.cn: 给树环剥就是剥一圈树皮，是腰带意象在林业里的用法。

normal.en: Remember the d in the middle: girdle keeps the d of its Old English form.
normal.cn: 记住中间的 d：girdle 保留了古英语词形里的 d。

abstract.en: Picture a leather strap pulled tight around a waist.
abstract.cn: 想象一条皮带被拉紧束在腰上。

abstract.en: Feel a stretchy band shaping the hips.
abstract.cn: 感觉一圈有弹性的带子收紧胯部。

abstract.en: See a ring of tall pines closing around a house.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈高大的松树把房子围起来。

examples.en: He loosened the girdle after the long ride.
examples.cn: 长途骑马之后，他松开了腰带。

examples.en: A girdle of lights surrounds the stadium at night.
examples.cn: 夜里一圈灯带围绕着体育场。

examples.en: The gardener girdled the trunk to stop new growth.
examples.cn: 园丁环剥了树干，阻止它继续长新枝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥兜」——像哥哥用一条带子把你的腰兜住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 gyrdel（腰带），源自原始日耳曼语 gurdlaz，与 gird（束）、girth（围长）同源，核心义是「把身体束住的一圈」，再引申为环带、环绕与环剥。

sensesIntro.en: Girdle starts as a waist belt, extends to a shaping garment, then to any ring around a thing, then to the verb of encircling, and finally to a ring cut in bark.
sensesIntro.cn: girdle 从腰间的带子开始，扩展到塑形内衣，再到任何绕成一圈的东西，再转为「环绕」的动词，最后指在树皮上刻出的一圈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strap drawn tight around a waist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被拉紧、束在腰上的带子。

branches.en: The waist belt is the original sense.
branches.cn: 腰间的带子是最初的义项。

branches.en: A shaping garment and any surrounding ring both come from gripping the body.
branches.cn: 塑形内衣与环绕的一圈都来自「把身体勒住」这一动作。

branches.en: The verb borrows the shape of the noun.
branches.cn: 动词沿用了名词的形状。

branches.en: The bark ring is a technical narrowing of the ring image.
branches.cn: 树皮上的一圈是「圈」这个意象在技术领域的收窄。

branches.en: A belt laid around the waist is the same ring that a river makes around a city.
branches.cn: 围在腰上的带子，与河流绕城的一圈是同一种「圈」。

intro.en: Girdle is a Germanic word with a very small family; English builds gird, begird, and girdling around it.
intro.cn: girdle 是日耳曼语源的词，词族很小；英语围绕它构成 gird、begird 与 girdling。

latinIntro.en: Girdle has no Latin ancestor: it belongs with the Germanic belt words, so no Latin cognates are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: girdle 没有拉丁语祖词：它属于日耳曼语的腰带词群，所以这里不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: Gird is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: gird 是名词背后的那个动词。

items.example: Gyrdel is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: gyrdel 是有记录的最早词形。

items.example: Gurdlaz is a reconstructed form.
items.exampleCN: gurdlaz 是重构形式。

items.example: Girdle keeps both the belt and ring senses.
items.exampleCN: girdle 同时保留腰带与环带两义。

items.example: Girth is a close relative of girdle.
items.exampleCN: girth 是 girdle 的近亲。

items.example: The prefix be- builds begird.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 be- 构成 begird。

items.example: Begird is now archaic but keeps the ring image.
items.exampleCN: begird 如今古旧，但保留了「围一圈」的意象。

items.meaning: the cutting of a bark ring
items.example: Girdling kills some trees slowly.
items.exampleCN: 环剥会让有些树慢慢枯死。

items.example: Ungird adds the negative prefix un-.
items.exampleCN: ungird 加了否定前缀 un-。

definition_zh: 要点；主旨；实质；大意
definition_en: the main point or substance of what is said or written
core_image: 写满字的一页纸上，被人用笔圈出的那一句
scene: 开会时大家说了很多，最后有人把结论写在白板中央。After an hour of talk, the chair summed up the gist in one sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 gist 是「要点」（第 1 个义项：说话或文字里最核心的意思）；句意：谈了一小时之后，主持人用一句话概括了要点。

derivatives.zh: 相邻的（拉丁语 jacere 意为「躺」，ad- 加 jacere 即「躺在旁边」，与 gist 同根）
弹出；驱逐（e- 加同根的 jacere，意为「扔出去」）
投射；伸出（pro- 加同根的 jacere，意为「向前扔」）

senses.title: The main point of what is said
senses.definition: the central idea that a speaker or writer wants to convey
senses.definitionCN: 说话人或作者想要传达的核心意思
senses.example: The gist of her talk was that the plan costs too much.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲话的要点是这个方案花费太高。
senses.why: The legal phrase the action lies gave the word its sense of the ground a thing rests on.
senses.whyCN: 法律短语「诉讼成立」给了这个词「事物所依托的根据」这一含义。

senses.title: The essential substance of a matter
senses.definition: the real substance of a problem or situation, apart from details
senses.definitionCN: 问题或局势的真正实质，撇开细枝末节
senses.example: Nobody had grasped the gist of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人抓住这场争执的实质。
senses.why: Once the word meant the ground of a case, it easily widened to the core of any matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指案件的依据，就很容易扩大到任何事情的核心。

senses.title: The legal ground of an action
senses.definition: the point on which a legal action rests, in older legal use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时法律用语中指诉讼所依据的要点
senses.example: The old plea stated the gist of the action.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的诉状写明了诉讼的根据。
senses.why: The source is the Old French form gist, it lies, said of a case that stands on a point.
senses.whyCN: 词源是古法语形式 gist（它成立、它躺着），用于说明案件立于某一点。

senses.title: A short summary that keeps the point
senses.definition: a brief account that keeps the main point without the details
senses.definitionCN: 保留要点而省略细节的简短叙述
senses.example: Just give me the gist and skip the examples.
senses.exampleCN: 只给我讲个大意，例子就跳过。
senses.why: If the gist is the core, then a summary of the core can also be called the gist.
senses.whyCN: 既然 gist 是核心，那么对核心的简述也可以叫 gist。

intro.en: Gist comes from Old French gist, it lies, a form of gesir, from Latin jacere, to lie; it began as a legal phrase about a case that lies.
intro.cn: gist 来自古法语 gist（它成立、它躺着），是 gesir 的一种形式，源于拉丁语 jacere（躺）；它最初是说明案件「成立」的法律短语。

items.en: Jacere means to lie down, and its compounds fill legal and everyday English.
items.cn: jacere 意为躺下，它的复合词遍布法律英语与日常英语。

items.en: Gesir means to lie, and its third-person form is gist.
items.cn: gesir 意为躺、成立，它的第三人称形式是 gist。

items.en: The phrase cest action gist says that the action lies, that it has grounds.
items.cn: 短语 cest action gist 意为「这一诉讼成立」，即它有依据。

items.en: English shortens the phrase to gist and moves it from the court to common speech.
items.cn: 英语把这个短语缩为 gist，并把它从法庭带入日常说法。

items.en: Modern English uses gist for the main point of any text or talk.
items.cn: 现代英语用 gist 指任何文字或谈话的要点。

note.en: Gist is a legal word turned general; its look-alikes are unrelated short words, and its near meanings are the core words of an argument.
note.cn: gist 是由法律用语转为通用词；形近词都是无关的短词，近义词是表达论点核心的词。

entries.definition: a joke or something said in fun
entries.definitionCN: 玩笑；笑话（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a sudden rush of wind
entries.definitionCN: 一阵狂风（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a closed hand
entries.definitionCN: 拳头（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the most important quality of a thing
the central difficulty of a problem
the real matter of what is said

normalIntro.en: Gist is a short word with a legal past, so its hooks come from courts, summaries, and its Latin root of lying.
normalIntro.cn: gist 是个短词，却有一段法律过往；记忆钩子来自法庭、摘要以及拉丁词根「躺」。

normal.en: The gist of a long speech fits into one sentence.
normal.cn: 长篇讲话的要点能装进一句话。

normal.en: To get the gist is to understand the main point, not every detail.
normal.cn: get the gist 指听懂要点，而不是每个细节。

normal.en: Latin jacere, to lie, also gives adjacent, eject, and project.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（躺）还给出 adjacent、eject 与 project。

normal.en: In old law, gist named the ground on which a case stood.
normal.cn: 在旧法律里，gist 指案件得以成立所依据的要点。

normal.en: Compare summary: a summary can be long, but the gist is only the core.
normal.cn: 对比 summary：摘要可以很长，而 gist 只是核心。

abstract.en: Watch a hand circle one sentence on a crowded page.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在密密麻麻的一页上圈出其中一句。

abstract.en: Feel the solid centre of a problem under its details.
abstract.cn: 想象一个问题在细节之下有一块坚硬的核。

abstract.en: See an old court clerk tapping the one line that decides the case.
abstract.cn: 想象旧时的法庭书记员点着那决定案件的一行字。

examples.en: She explained the gist of the report in two minutes.
examples.cn: 她用两分钟说明了报告的要旨。

examples.en: I did not catch every word, but I got the gist.
examples.cn: 我没有听清每个字，但明白了大意。

examples.en: The gist of his complaint was the noise at night.
examples.cn: 他抱怨的实质是夜里的噪声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「记死它」——把要点记死，就抓住了 gist；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 gist（它成立、它躺着）源于拉丁语 jacere（躺），经法律短语「诉讼得以成立之点」进入英语，16 世纪缩为 gist，再由「案件的依据」引申为「要点、实质」。

sensesIntro.en: Gist begins as the legal ground of a case, widens to the substance of any matter, keeps a technical sense in law, and finally names a short summary of the core.
sensesIntro.cn: gist 从案件的诉讼依据开始，扩大到任何事情的要害，在法律里保留一个专门义项，最后指对核心的简短概括。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sentence circled on a crowded page.
core.cn: 核心意象：在写满字的一页上圈出的那一句。

branches.en: The main point of speech is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 说话的核心意思是日常义项。

branches.en: The substance of a matter is the widened legal ground.
branches.cn: 事情的实质是扩大后的「法律依据」。

branches.en: The law keeps the original technical sense.
branches.cn: 法律保留了最初的技术义项。

branches.en: A summary is the main point cut down to size.
branches.cn: 梗概是被压缩到最小的要点。

branches.en: A summary and the main point differ only in length.
branches.cn: 梗概与要点只差在长短。

intro.en: Gist has almost no English suffixes of its own; its structure is a Latin root of lying plus prefixes that build a large family.
intro.cn: gist 本身几乎没有英语后缀；它的结构是一个意为「躺」的拉丁词根，加上构成大词族的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere, to lie or to throw, is the root; its participle jacens means lying.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（躺、投掷）是这个词根，它的分词 jacens 意为「躺着的」。

items.example: The prefix ad- builds adjacent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 构成 adjacent。

items.example: The prefix e- builds eject.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 构成 eject。

items.example: The prefix pro- builds project.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 构成 project。

items.example: Jacere is the root of the legal phrase.
items.exampleCN: jacere 是那个法律短语的词根。

items.example: Jacens gives the image of something lying in place.
items.exampleCN: jacens 给出「躺在那里」的意象。

items.example: Gesir carries the root into French.
items.exampleCN: gesir 把这个词根带入法语。

items.example: Gist is the shortened legal phrase.
items.exampleCN: gist 是缩短后的法律短语。

items.example: Adjacent keeps the literal sense of lying near.
items.exampleCN: adjacent 保留「躺在旁边」的字面义。

items.example: Project uses the throwing sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: project 用的是词根「投掷」的那一面。

definition_zh: 魅力；诱惑力；浮华；（古）魔法
definition_en: an attractive, exciting quality that makes people admire someone or something
core_image: 舞台灯光下，一个人被金色的光包围
scene: 电影首映的红毯上，闪光灯把明星照得通身发亮。The premiere gave the young actress a taste of Hollywood glamor.
sceneCN: 这里 glamor 是「魅力」（第 1 个义项：让人仰慕的吸引力）；句意：这次首映让年轻女演员尝到了好莱坞式的魅力。

derivatives.zh: 有魅力的（glamor 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成）
使显得迷人；美化（glamor 加动词后缀 -ize 构成）
美化；渲染（glamorize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成）

senses.title: An alluring charm
senses.definition: a quality that makes someone or something seem exciting and worth admiring
senses.definitionCN: 让某人或某物显得激动人心、令人仰慕的特质
senses.example: The old hotel still has the glamor of another era.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老酒店仍带着另一个时代的魅力。
senses.why: The word started as a name for magic, so charm that casts a spell became the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指魔法，所以「像施了咒一样的吸引力」成了第一个义项。

senses.title: The artificial shine of fame and wealth
senses.definition: the exciting, often exaggerated appeal of wealth, fame, and show business
senses.definitionCN: 财富、名声与演艺圈那种常被夸大的吸引力
senses.example: Behind the glamor of the awards lies a lot of hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖礼的浮华背后是大量辛苦工作。
senses.why: Magic became stage magic, and stage magic became the glitter around famous people.
senses.whyCN: 魔法变成舞台魔术，舞台魔术又变成名人周围的光彩。

senses.title: Enchantment or magic, in older use
senses.definition: a spell or magical influence, in older literary use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文学用语中的咒语或魔法力量
senses.example: The witch cast a glamor over the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 女巫对整个村子施了魔法。
senses.why: The oldest sense is magical: a glamor was a spell that changed how things looked.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是魔法：glamor 是一种改变事物外观的咒语。

senses.title: A glamorous style of dress and display
senses.definition: a romantic, decorative style of dress or presentation
senses.definitionCN: 浪漫而带装饰性的着装或呈现风格
senses.example: She dressed with the glamor of a silent-film star.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿得像默片明星那样华丽迷人。
senses.why: Once the word named an exciting quality, it could also name the style that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指一种动人的特质后，它也指制造这种特质的风格。

intro.en: Glamor is the American spelling of glamour, which began as a Scots form of grammar: learning, then occult learning, then magic, then charm.
intro.cn: glamor 是 glamour 的美式拼法；glamour 最初是 grammar 的苏格兰变体，由「学问」到「秘术」，再到「魔法」，最后到「魅力」。

items.en: Grammatica means the study of letters, and it passes into French as gramaire.
items.cn: grammatica 意为「字母之学」，经法语 gramaire 传入。

items.en: Scots speakers use glamer for magical influence, a variant of grammar.
items.cn: 苏格兰语用 glamer 指魔法般的影响力，它是 grammar 的变体。

items.en: English takes up glamour as the literary word for enchantment.
items.cn: 英语把 glamour 吸收为文学中表示「迷惑」的词。

items.en: The sense shifts from spells to the charm of famous people and fashion.
items.cn: 词义从咒语转向名人与时尚的光彩。

items.en: American English writes the word as glamor and keeps glamour as the British form.
items.cn: 美式英语把这个词写作 glamor，而 glamour 保留为英式拼法。

note.en: Glamor is the American noun; its look-alikes are the British spelling, the adjective, and the verb, and its near meanings are charm words.
note.cn: glamor 是美式拼法的名词；形近词是英式拼法、形容词与动词，近义词是表示「魅力」的词。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same noun
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写

entries.definition: full of glamor
to make something seem more attractive
the power to please or attract
a mysterious attractive quality
the quality of being interesting or attractive

normalIntro.en: Glamor is magic that became style: its hooks run from grammar to spells to red-carpet light.
normalIntro.cn: glamor 是由魔法变成的风格：记忆线索从 grammar 到咒语，再到红毯的灯光。

normal.en: Glamour and grammar are the same word in origin, one bookish, one dazzling.
normal.cn: glamour 与 grammar 同源：一个书卷气，一个耀眼。

normal.en: The British spelling keeps the u as glamour, while the American drops it as glamor.
normal.cn: 英式保留 u 写作 glamour，美式去掉 u 写作 glamor。

normal.en: A glamor shot is a photograph made to flatter the sitter.
normal.cn: glamor shot 是拍来美化被摄者的照片。

normal.en: Glamorize means to make something look better than it is.
normal.cn: glamorize 指把某物弄得比实际更好看。

normal.en: The phrase Hollywood glamor covers the shine of film stars.
normal.cn: Hollywood glamor 这个说法涵盖影星身上的光彩。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight making one person glow on a dark stage.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯让一个人在昏暗的舞台上发光。

abstract.en: See the gold lights of an award show hiding tired workers.
abstract.cn: 想象颁奖礼的金色灯光遮住了疲惫的工作人员。

abstract.en: Imagine an old woman in a story drawing a glowing circle in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象故事里的老妇人在空中画出一个发光的圆圈。

examples.en: The magazine sells glamor more than news.
examples.cn: 这本杂志卖的是魅力，而不是新闻。

examples.en: He was drawn to the glamor of the racing world.
examples.cn: 他被赛车界的魅力吸引。

examples.en: Old Hollywood glamor still shapes fashion today.
examples.cn: 旧日好莱坞的浮华至今仍在影响时尚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥拉莫」——像有人把你拉住不放，被魅力拽住了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: glamour 是 grammar 的苏格兰变体：拉丁语 grammatica（字母之学）→ 古法语 gramaire → 苏格兰语 glamer（秘术）→ 英语 glamour（魔法）→ 现代义「魅力、浮华」；美式拼作 glamor。

sensesIntro.en: In origin glamor is magic; in modern use the charm comes first, then the shine of fame, then the older magic sense, then the style built on that charm.
sensesIntro.cn: glamor 在词源上是魔法；现代用法先指魅力，再指名气的光彩，然后是较旧的魔法义，最后指由这种魅力造出的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure lit by gold stage light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被金色舞台灯光笼罩的人。

branches.en: The charm sense is the modern centre of the word.
branches.cn: 魅力义是现代用法的中心。

branches.en: The shine of fame is charm attached to money and cameras.
branches.cn: 名气的光彩是把魅力绑在金钱与镜头上。

branches.en: The magic sense is the oldest layer, still alive in literature.
branches.cn: 魔法义是最古老的一层，在文学里仍活着。

branches.en: The style sense names the surface that produces the charm.
branches.cn: 风格义指制造这种魅力的表面效果。

branches.en: A star can have personal charm and borrowed shine at once.
branches.cn: 明星可以同时拥有个人魅力与借来的光彩。

intro.en: Glamor keeps the bare noun; English builds glamorous, glamorously, glamorize, and glamorization on top of it.
intro.cn: glamor 保留光秃的名词形式；英语在它上面构成 glamorous、glamorously、glamorize 与 glamorization。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor is grammatica, the study of letters, which reached Scots through French gramaire.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁语祖词是 grammatica（字母之学），经法语 gramaire 传入苏格兰语。

items.example: Grammatica is the remote source of the word.
items.exampleCN: grammatica 是这个词的远源。

items.example: Gramaire carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: gramaire 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Glamer is the Scots form with the magic sense.
items.exampleCN: glamer 是带魔法义的苏格兰语形式。

items.example: Glamour is the British spelling.
items.exampleCN: glamour 是英式拼法。

items.example: Glamor drops the u in American English.
items.exampleCN: 美式英语里的 glamor 去掉了 u。

items.example: The suffix -ous builds glamorous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 glamorous。

items.example: Glamorous describes a person or a life.
items.exampleCN: glamorous 描述人或生活。

items.example: The suffix -ize builds glamorize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 glamorize。

items.example: Glamorize turns a plain thing into a shiny one.
items.exampleCN: glamorize 把平凡之物变得光鲜。

items.example: Glamorization adds -ation to the verb.
items.exampleCN: glamorization 在动词后加了 -ation。

definition_zh: 有魅力的；迷人的；光鲜的
definition_en: exciting and attractive in a way that seems special or rich
core_image: 被聚光灯照着、浑身发亮的人
scene: 颁奖礼的红毯上，记者的镜头全都对准同一个人。Every camera on the red carpet turned toward the glamorous singer.
sceneCN: 这里 glamorous 是「有魅力的」（第 1 个义项：让人仰慕的吸引力）；句意：红毯上所有镜头都转向那位迷人的歌手。

pos.zh: 有魅力的；迷人的；光鲜的

derivatives.zh: 迷人地（glamorous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成）
魅力；迷人之处（glamorous 加名词后缀 -ness 构成）
使显得迷人；美化（与 glamorous 同出 glamour 的词族）

senses.title: Full of exciting charm
senses.definition: having a quality that makes people admire and want to be near
senses.definitionCN: 具有让人仰慕、想要靠近的特质
senses.example: The city looks glamorous from the top of the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 从塔顶看，这座城市显得很有魅力。
senses.why: The suffix -ous means full of, so glamorous is literally full of glamor.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ous 意为「充满」，所以 glamorous 字面就是「充满魅力」。

senses.title: Rich, famous, and exciting
senses.titleCN: 富贵而刺激的；令人向往的
senses.definition: marked by wealth, fame, and excitement rather than ordinary life
senses.definitionCN: 以财富、名声与刺激为标志，而非平凡生活
senses.example: They lived a glamorous life of parties and travel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们过着派对与旅行交织的迷人生活。
senses.why: Because glamor gathered around film stars and wealth, the adjective took on their shine.
senses.whyCN: 因为 glamor 围绕影星与财富聚集，这个形容词也就带上了那层光彩。

senses.title: Magical, in older use
senses.definition: enchanted or magical, in older literary use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文学用语中表示「受了魔法、有魔力的」
senses.example: The glamorous ring was said to change its wearer.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那枚有魔力的戒指能改变佩戴它的人。
senses.why: The oldest noun sense was a spell, so the adjective once meant full of magic.
senses.whyCN: 名词最古老的义项是咒语，所以形容词也曾表示「充满魔力的」。

senses.title: Elegantly stylish in appearance
senses.definition: elegantly and strikingly dressed or presented
senses.definitionCN: 穿着或呈现得优雅而出众
senses.example: She arrived in a glamorous black gown.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着一条迷人的黑色长裙到场。
senses.why: Style is how glamor shows on the surface, so the adjective also describes the look.
senses.whyCN: 风格是 glamor 在表面的显现，所以形容词也用来描述外表。

intro.en: Glamorous is glamour plus the suffix -ous, and glamour itself began as a Scots form of grammar.
intro.cn: glamorous 是 glamour 加后缀 -ous 构成，而 glamour 最初是 grammar 的苏格兰变体。

items.en: Grammatica, the study of letters, is the remote source.
items.cn: grammatica（字母之学）是它的远源。

items.en: Glamer names magical influence, a variant of grammar.
items.cn: glamer 指魔法般的影响力，是 grammar 的变体。

items.en: Glamour becomes the literary word for enchantment, and -ous joins it.
items.cn: glamour 成为文学中表示「迷惑」的词，后缀 -ous 也加在它后面。

items.en: The suffix -ous, from Latin -osus, means full of and makes glamorous.
items.cn: 后缀 -ous 源自拉丁语 -osus，意为「充满」，由此构成 glamorous。

items.en: The adjective moves from magic to the shine of famous people.
items.cn: 这个形容词从魔法义转向名人身上的光彩。

items.en: Modern English uses glamorous for anyone or anything that looks rich and exciting.
items.cn: 现代英语用 glamorous 形容任何看起来富贵而刺激的人或物。

note.en: Glamorous is the adjective of glamour; its look-alikes are the noun spellings and its adverb, and its near meanings are charm adjectives.
note.cn: glamorous 是 glamour 的形容词；形近词是名词的两种拼法与它的副词，近义词是表示「迷人」的形容词。

entries.definition: the British noun form behind the adjective
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的英式名词形式

entries.definition: the American noun form behind the adjective
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的美式名词形式

entries.definition: in a glamorous way
pleasing and attractive
attractive in a mysterious way
attractive in a flashy way

normalIntro.en: Glamorous is glamour plus -ous, full of charm; its hooks are the suffix, the noun family, and the red-carpet scene.
normalIntro.cn: glamorous 是 glamour 加 -ous，意为「充满魅力」；记忆钩子是后缀、名词词族与红毯场景。

normal.en: The suffix -ous means full of, so glamorous is full of glamour.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ous 意为「充满」，所以 glamorous 就是「充满魅力」。

normal.en: Drop -ous and you have the noun glamour, the charm itself.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ous 就得到名词 glamour，也就是魅力本身。

normal.en: The adverb glamorously adds -ly to say how someone arrives.
normal.cn: 副词 glamorously 加上 -ly，用来说明某人以怎样的姿态到场。

normal.en: Glamorous describes looks and lives, not quiet virtues.
normal.cn: glamorous 描述外表与生活，不描述安静的美德。

normal.en: Remember the pair: glamour is the thing, glamorous is the quality.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：glamour 是那个东西，glamorous 是那种性质。

abstract.en: See one face held inside a bright circle of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸被一圈明亮的光圈罩住。

abstract.en: Picture gold lights and tired workers in the same hall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一座大厅里有金色灯光和疲惫的工作人员。

abstract.en: Think of an old ring glowing on a velvet cushion.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚旧戒指在天鹅绒垫子上发光。

examples.en: The hotel lobby felt glamorous after the renovation.
examples.cn: 翻新之后，酒店大堂显得很有魅力。

examples.en: She wanted a glamorous job in fashion.
examples.cn: 她想要一份时尚界的风光职业。

examples.en: Photographs make even ordinary streets look glamorous.
examples.cn: 照片能让再普通的街道也显得迷人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥拉莫若斯」——读起来像一串闪光的碎响，正配「迷人」的意思；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: glamour（魅力）加形容词后缀 -ous（充满……的）；glamour 又是 grammar 的苏格兰变体，经「学问→秘术→魔法→魅力」的演变，美式名词拼作 glamor。

sensesIntro.en: Glamorous keeps the charm sense first, then the shine of wealth and fame, then the old magic sense, and last the stylish look.
sensesIntro.cn: glamorous 先保留「魅力」义，再指财富与名声的光彩，然后是旧的魔法义，最后指时髦的外表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lit by a spotlight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被聚光灯照亮的脸。

branches.en: The charm sense is the everyday centre.
branches.cn: 魅力义是日常用法的中心。

branches.en: Wealth and fame add a borrowed shine.
branches.cn: 财富与名声为它添上一层借来的光彩。

branches.en: The magic sense survives from the oldest layer of the noun.
branches.cn: 魔法义从名词最古老的一层留存下来。

branches.en: The look is the visible surface of the quality.
branches.cn: 外表是这种特质可见的表面。

branches.en: A charming person and a stylish one can be called by the same word.
branches.cn: 有魅力的人与穿着时髦的人可以用同一个词形容。

intro.en: Glamorous is a suffixed adjective; English builds glamorously, glamorousness, and glamorize around it.
intro.cn: glamorous 是加后缀构成的形容词；英语围绕它构成 glamorously、glamorousness 与 glamorize。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are -osus, meaning full of, and grammatica, the study of letters, behind the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁成分是表示「充满」的 -osus，以及名词背后的 grammatica（字母之学）。

items.example: Glamour is the noun under the adjective.
items.exampleCN: glamour 是形容词底下的名词。

items.example: Glamor is the American spelling.
items.exampleCN: glamor 是美式拼法。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The Latin suffix -osus is the source of -ous.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁后缀 -osus 是 -ous 的来源。

items.example: Glamorous keeps the -ous suffix visibly.
items.exampleCN: glamorous 明显保留着 -ous 后缀。

items.example: The suffix -ly builds glamorously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 glamorously。

items.example: Glamorously describes the way she entered.
items.exampleCN: glamorously 描述她进场的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness builds glamorousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 glamorousness。

items.example: Glamorousness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: glamorousness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Glamorize shares the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: glamorize 共享同一个名词词干。

definition_zh: 腺；腺体；淋巴结（口语中常用复数）
definition_en: an organ or group of cells that makes and releases a substance such as a hormone
core_image: 身体深处一小团圆形组织，不断把分泌物送出去
scene: 体检时，医生用指尖轻按颈部，检查甲状腺是否肿大。The doctor pressed the neck gently to check the thyroid gland.
sceneCN: 这里 gland 是「腺体」（第 1 个义项：制造并释放激素的器官）；句意：医生轻按颈部，检查甲状腺是否肿大。

derivatives.zh: 由 gland 加 -ular 构成，义为「腺的；腺体的」
由 gland 加 -less 构成，义为「没有腺体的」
由 gland 加指小后缀 -ule 构成，义为「小腺体」

senses.title: A hormone-secreting organ
senses.definition: an organ that makes hormones and releases them into the blood
senses.definitionCN: 制造激素并把激素释放进血液的器官
senses.example: The thyroid gland controls how fast the body uses energy.
senses.exampleCN: 甲状腺控制身体消耗能量的速度。
senses.why: Glans first meant an acorn, and the small round organ took its name from that shape.
senses.whyCN: glans 最初指橡子，这种小而圆的器官因形状相似而得名。

senses.title: A gland with a duct
senses.definition: an organ that makes a liquid and sends it out through a duct
senses.definitionCN: 制造液体并通过导管把它排出体外的器官
senses.example: Sweat glands in the skin release water when the body overheats.
senses.exampleCN: 身体过热时，皮肤里的汗腺会排出水分。
senses.why: The same small factory image covers organs whose product leaves the body instead of the blood.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「小工厂」意象也适用于产物排出体外、而不是进入血液的器官。

senses.title: A lymph node
senses.definition: a lymph node, especially one that is swollen during an infection
senses.definitionCN: 淋巴结，尤指感染时肿大起来的淋巴结
senses.example: Her glands felt tender when she swallowed.
senses.exampleCN: 她吞咽时觉得淋巴结一碰就疼。
senses.why: A swollen node in the neck feels like a small lump, so everyday speech calls it a gland.
senses.whyCN: 颈部肿大的淋巴结摸起来像一个小团块，所以日常口语把它叫作 gland。

senses.title: A special gland in an animal
senses.definition: a small organ in an animal that produces a particular substance such as scent, venom, or silk
senses.definitionCN: 动物体内制造特定物质的小器官，如气味、毒液或丝
senses.example: The musk deer has a scent gland that produces a strong odour.
senses.exampleCN: 麝鹿有一个能产生强烈气味的气味腺。
senses.why: Animals evolved many small chemical factories, and English extends the organ word to all of them.
senses.whyCN: 动物演化出许多小小的「化学工厂」，英语把这个器官词扩展到所有这些结构。

senses.title: A secreting structure in a plant
senses.definition: a cell or hair on a plant that releases a substance such as nectar or oil
senses.definitionCN: 植物体上释放花蜜或油脂等物质的细胞或毛状结构
senses.example: Glands on the leaf surface give the herb its strong smell.
senses.exampleCN: 叶片表面的腺体让这种香草带有浓烈的气味。
senses.why: Plants also have tiny secretory points, so the shape word moved from bodies to leaves.
senses.whyCN: 植物也有微小的分泌点，于是这个表形状的词从动物身体扩展到了叶片。

intro.en: Gland comes through Old French from Latin glans, an acorn, and its diminutive glandula, a small gland.
intro.cn: gland 经古法语来自拉丁语 glans（橡子）及其指小形式 glandula（小腺体）。

items.en: Glans means an acorn, and it also names a small round body.
items.cn: glans 意为橡子，也指小而圆的器官。

items.en: Glandula is the diminutive of glans, a little acorn or a small gland.
items.cn: glandula 是 glans 的指小形式，意为小橡子或小腺体。

items.en: Glandre names a gland or a swollen node in Old French.
items.cn: 古法语 glandre 指腺体或肿大的结节。

items.en: Middle English glandre covers both secreting organs and lymph nodes.
items.cn: 中古英语 glandre 既指分泌器官，也指淋巴结。

items.en: Modern English shortens the form to gland and keeps both senses.
items.cn: 现代英语把词形缩短为 gland，并保留两种含义。

note.en: Gland belongs to the Latin acorn family, and it shares a semantic field with organ, hormone, and node.
note.cn: gland 属于拉丁语「橡子」词族，并与 organ、hormone、node 同处一个语义场。

entries.definition: relating to a gland or glands
having no glands
a small gland or a gland-like structure
a part of the body that has a special function
a chemical made by a gland and carried in the blood
a small lump of tissue, such as a lymph node

normalIntro.en: Gland is a small factory in the body, named after the acorn it resembles.
normalIntro.cn: gland 是身体里的小工厂，名字来自它像橡子的形状。

normal.en: Thyroid gland and adrenal gland are common collocations.
normal.cn: thyroid gland（甲状腺）与 adrenal gland（肾上腺）都是常见搭配。

normal.en: The plural glands often means the lymph nodes in the neck.
normal.cn: 复数 glands 常指颈部的淋巴结。

normal.en: Glandular adds -ular and means relating to glands.
normal.cn: glandular 加了 -ular，表示与腺体有关。

normal.en: Glandless adds -less and means without glands.
normal.cn: glandless 加了 -less，表示没有腺体。

normal.en: Latin glans, an acorn, explains the round shape in the image.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 glans（橡子）解释了意象里的圆形。

abstract.en: See a tiny round factory under the skin, dropping hormones into a stream.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤下一个小小的圆形工厂，把激素滴进一条溪流。

abstract.en: See a sweat gland as a small pump pushing water out through a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象汗腺是一台小水泵，通过管道把水推出去。

abstract.en: See a swollen lymph node in the neck as a small acorn under the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象颈部肿大的淋巴结是皮下的一颗小橡子。

examples.en: The thyroid gland produces hormones that regulate growth.
examples.cn: 甲状腺产生调节生长的激素。

examples.en: Her neck glands were swollen, so the doctor checked them.
examples.cn: 她颈部的淋巴结肿了，所以医生做了检查。

examples.en: The nectar glands of the plant attract ants that protect it.
examples.cn: 这种植物的花蜜腺吸引蚂蚁来保护它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格兰德」——读音像「grand」，可联想身体里一座小小的腺体工厂；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 glans（橡子；圆形小体）→ 指小形式 glandula（小腺体）→ 古法语 glandre → 英语 gland，核心义「像橡子一样的小团块」。

sensesIntro.en: Gland begins with the organs that make hormones, moves to ducted glands, and then to lymph nodes and the small secretory structures of animals and plants.
sensesIntro.cn: gland 先指制造激素的器官，再指有导管的腺体，然后扩展到淋巴结以及动物和植物的微小分泌结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small round factory hidden inside the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体里一座隐蔽的小圆形工厂。

branches.en: Endocrine glands are the core medical sense.
branches.cn: 内分泌腺是核心的医学义项。

branches.en: Ducted glands send fluid out of the body.
branches.cn: 有导管的腺体把液体排出体外。

branches.en: Swollen lymph nodes are the everyday plural use.
branches.cn: 肿大的淋巴结是日常口语中的复数用法。

branches.en: Both are organs that release a product.
branches.cn: 两者都是释放某种产物的器官。

branches.en: Nodes and plant glands are small secretory lumps.
branches.cn: 淋巴结与植物腺体都是微小的分泌团块。

intro.en: Gland is a Latin word carried through French, and English has built glandular, glandless, and glandule on it.
intro.cn: gland 是经法语传入的拉丁语词，英语围绕它构成了 glandular、glandless 与 glandule。

latinIntro.en: Latin glans means an acorn, and glandula, its diminutive, means a small gland.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 glans 意为橡子，其指小形式 glandula 意为小腺体。

items.example: Glans supplies the round acorn image.
items.exampleCN: glans 提供橡子般的圆形意象。

items.example: Glandula is the diminutive that names a gland.
items.exampleCN: glandula 是指小形式，用来指腺体。

items.example: Glandre carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: glandre 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Gland keeps the medical sense.
items.exampleCN: gland 保留医学含义。

items.example: The suffix -ular forms glandular.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ular 构成 glandular。

items.example: The suffix -ular marks a relation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ular 表示关联。

items.example: The suffix -less forms glandless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 glandless。

items.example: Glandule keeps the diminutive idea.
items.exampleCN: glandule 保留了指小的意味。

items.example: The suffix -less removes a quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 表示缺少某种性质。

definition_zh: 玻璃器皿；玻璃制品（总称）
definition_en: articles made of glass, especially drinking vessels, dishes, and containers
core_image: 橱柜里一排透明杯盘，灯光穿过时折出细碎亮斑
scene: 搬家前，她把每一只玻璃杯和盘子都用软纸包好。She wrapped every piece of glassware in soft paper before the movers came.
sceneCN: 这里 glassware 是「玻璃器皿」（第 1 个义项：玻璃制成的器皿总称）；句意：搬家工人来之前，她用软纸把每一件玻璃器皿都包好了。

derivatives.zh: glassware 的前半部分，义为「玻璃」
由 glass 加 -y 构成，义为「玻璃般的；光滑的」
由 glass 加 maker 构成，义为「玻璃工匠」
由 glass 加 blowing 构成，义为「吹制玻璃」

senses.title: Glass articles as a class
senses.definition: objects made of glass when they are considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类物品来考虑的玻璃制品
senses.example: The shelves were crowded with glassware of every size.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上摆满了各种大小的玻璃器皿。
senses.why: Ware means goods, so glassware is the whole class of goods made of glass.
senses.whyCN: ware 意为货物，所以 glassware 就是玻璃制成的整类物品。

senses.title: Table glass
senses.definition: glasses used for drinking or for serving food at a table
senses.definitionCN: 餐桌上用来饮酒或盛放食物的玻璃器皿
senses.example: She set out the glassware before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到来之前，她把玻璃器皿摆好了。
senses.why: The table is where glass goods are most often used, so the word often points there.
senses.whyCN: 餐桌是玻璃器皿最常出现的地方，所以这个词常指向餐桌用具。

senses.title: Laboratory and industrial glass
senses.titleCN: 实验室与工业玻璃器具
senses.definition: glass containers and instruments made for scientific or factory use
senses.definitionCN: 为科研或工厂使用而制造的玻璃容器与器具
senses.example: The technician rinsed the glassware after the test.
senses.exampleCN: 测试结束后，技术员冲洗了玻璃器具。
senses.why: Science needs clear, heat-resistant vessels, and the word expands to cover them.
senses.whyCN: 科研需要透明且耐热的容器，于是这个词的范围扩展到了这些器具。

senses.title: One glass article
senses.definition: a single object made of glass
senses.definitionCN: 单独的一件玻璃制品
senses.example: One piece of glassware slipped from her hand and broke.
senses.exampleCN: 一件玻璃器皿从她手中滑落摔碎了。
senses.why: A mass noun is counted through a piece of, and the word then names one object.
senses.whyCN: 物质名词借助 a piece of 来计数，这时这个词就指单独一件物品。

senses.title: Decorative glass
senses.definition: glass objects valued for their design rather than for daily use
senses.definitionCN: 因设计而受重视、并非日常使用的玻璃制品
senses.example: The museum shows glassware from the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出了十九世纪的玻璃器皿。
senses.why: Fine glass becomes art, and the word follows it into collections and museums.
senses.whyCN: 精美的玻璃成为艺术品，这个词也随之进入收藏与博物馆语境。

intro.en: Glassware joins two Old English words, glæs for glass and waru for goods.
intro.cn: glassware 由两个古英语词构成：glæs 指玻璃，waru 指货物。

items.en: A reconstructed root, usually written *glasą, names a bright transparent material.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *glasą 指明亮透明的材料。

items.en: Glæs means glass, and waru means goods or merchandise.
items.cn: glæs 指玻璃，waru 指货物或商品。

items.en: Glas and ware are common nouns that can be joined in compounds.
items.cn: 中古英语里 glas 与 ware 都是常用名词，可以组合成复合词。

items.en: Glassware becomes the collective name for articles made of glass.
items.cn: glassware 成为玻璃制品的集合名称。

items.en: Laboratory and industrial uses widen the class of glassware.
items.cn: 实验室与工业用途扩大了 glassware 所指的范围。

note.en: Glassware is a compound of glass and ware, and it sits near crockery, porcelain, and crystal in the tableware field.
note.cn: glassware 是 glass 与 ware 的复合词，在餐具义场中与 crockery、porcelain、crystal 相邻。

entries.definition: the hard transparent material
entries.definitionCN: 玻璃这种坚硬透明的材料

entries.definition: like glass, smooth and shiny
a person who makes glass
plates, dishes, and cups, usually made of clay
entries.definitionCN: 通常为陶制的盘碟杯具

entries.definition: a hard white material used for fine dishes
entries.definitionCN: 精细瓷器所用的坚硬白色材料

entries.definition: high-quality clear glass

normalIntro.en: Glassware is glass plus ware: ware means goods, so the word is simply glass goods.
normalIntro.cn: glassware 就是 glass 加 ware：ware 意为货物，所以这个词就是玻璃制品。

normal.en: Ware appears in tableware, hardware, and software, all meaning kinds of goods.
normal.cn: ware 出现在 tableware、hardware、software 里，都表示某类物品。

normal.en: Glassware is usually uncountable, so one says a piece of glassware.
normal.cn: glassware 通常不可数，所以说 a piece of glassware。

normal.en: Glassmaker and glassblowing name the people and craft behind glassware.
normal.cn: glassmaker 与 glassblowing 指制造玻璃器皿的人与工艺。

normal.en: Laboratory glassware must resist heat and chemicals.
normal.cn: 实验室玻璃器皿必须耐热并耐化学腐蚀。

normal.en: Crockery is the clay cousin of glassware.
normal.cn: crockery 是 glassware 的陶制近亲。

abstract.en: See a shelf of clear cups shining under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一层架子上摆满透明杯子，在灯下泛光。

abstract.en: See a dinner table set with tall stemmed glasses.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌上摆好了高脚杯。

abstract.en: See a lab bench lined with beakers and flasks.
abstract.cn: 想象实验台上排着烧杯和烧瓶。

examples.en: She packed the glassware carefully before the move.
examples.cn: 搬家前她小心地把玻璃器皿包好。

examples.en: The laboratory keeps its glassware in locked cabinets.
examples.cn: 实验室把玻璃器具锁在柜子里。

examples.en: A piece of glassware broke when it hit the floor.
examples.cn: 一件玻璃器皿掉到地上摔碎了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥拉丝碗」——读音近似「glass ware」，可联想一只透明玻璃碗；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 glæs（玻璃）+ waru（货物、器皿）→ 中古英语 glas 与 ware → 现代英语 glassware，核心义「玻璃制成的器皿」。

sensesIntro.en: Glassware first names glass goods as a class, then the glass used at a table, then laboratory glass, a single article, and finally decorative glass.
sensesIntro.cn: glassware 先指作为一类的玻璃制品，再指餐桌上的玻璃器皿、实验室器具、单件器皿，最后指装饰性玻璃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of clear vessels catching the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：架子上排着透明的器皿，接住灯光。

branches.en: The class of glass goods is the base sense.
branches.cn: 玻璃制品这一整类是基础义项。

branches.en: Table use is the everyday setting.
branches.cn: 餐桌用途是最日常的场景。

branches.en: Laboratory glass is a technical extension.
branches.cn: 实验室玻璃是技术领域的延伸。

branches.en: A single article is the countable use.
branches.cn: 单件器皿是可数用法。

branches.en: Decorated glass is still glass goods, valued for design.
branches.cn: 装饰玻璃仍属玻璃制品，只是价值在设计与收藏。

intro.en: Glassware is an English compound of two Old English nouns, glass and ware, with a family around each part.
intro.cn: glassware 是由 glass 与 ware 两个古英语名词构成的英语复合词，两部分各自都有词族。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin; Latin vitrum means glass but is not a source of glassware.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语而非拉丁语；拉丁语 vitrum 意为玻璃，但不是 glassware 的来源。

items.example: Glæs is the Old English word for glass.
items.exampleCN: glæs 是古英语中表示玻璃的词。

items.example: Glass is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: glass 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Waru is the Old English source of ware.
items.exampleCN: waru 是 ware 的古英语来源。

definition_zh: 微光；闪光；闪烁；隐约显现
definition_en: a soft or brief light, or to shine with such a light
core_image: 黑夜中一束细光在光滑表面上轻轻滑过
scene: 停电的夜里，走廊尽头有一线微光从门缝下透出来。On the night of the power cut, a faint gleam came under the door at the end of the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 gleam 是「微光」（第 1 个义项：柔和而短暂的光）；句意：停电的夜里，走廊尽头有一线微光从门缝下透出来。

derivatives.zh: 由 gleam 加 -ing 构成，义为「闪耀的」
由 gleam 加 -y 构成，义为「发微光的」

senses.title: A soft or brief light
senses.definition: a small amount of light that shines softly or for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 柔和地或短暂地照出的一小片光
senses.example: A gleam of light showed under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门下透出一线微光。
senses.why: The Old English noun named brightness, so the first sense is simply a patch of light.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词本义是明亮，所以第一个义项就是一小片光。

senses.title: Reflected shine
senses.definition: light reflected from a smooth or wet surface
senses.definitionCN: 从光滑或潮湿表面反射出来的光
senses.example: She polished the silver until it had a warm gleam.
senses.exampleCN: 她把银器擦到泛出温暖的光泽。
senses.why: Smooth surfaces throw light back, and the word names that returned shine.
senses.whyCN: 光滑表面会把光反射回来，这个词就指这种被送回来的亮光。

senses.title: A faint trace of a feeling
senses.definition: a small sign of a quality or feeling that is just beginning to appear
senses.definitionCN: 某种品质或情绪刚刚显露的一点点迹象
senses.example: There was a gleam of hope in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音里有一丝希望。
senses.why: A tiny light becomes a metaphor for a small amount of anything good.
senses.whyCN: 一点点光被用作比喻，指任何美好事物的一小部分。

senses.title: A bright look in the eyes
senses.definition: a bright or intense look in the eyes that shows an emotion
senses.definitionCN: 眼中流露情绪的一种明亮而强烈的神情
senses.example: A gleam of mischief appeared in her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她眼里闪过一丝顽皮的光。
senses.why: Eyes reflect light, and a bright eye has long signalled strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛会反光，明亮的眼睛一直被视为强烈情绪的讯号。

senses.title: To shine softly
senses.definition: to shine with a soft or unsteady light
senses.definitionCN: 以柔和或不稳定的光发亮
senses.example: The moon gleamed through the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮透过云层发出微光。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to give off the light that gleam names.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，表示发出 gleam 所指的那种光。

senses.title: To reflect light
senses.definition: to reflect light from a surface, especially a wet or polished one
senses.definitionCN: 从表面反光，尤指潮湿或打磨过的表面
senses.example: The wet stones gleamed after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后湿漉漉的石头闪着光。
senses.why: A surface that returns light can be said to gleam like the light itself.
senses.whyCN: 能把光送回来的表面，也像光本身一样可以说在 gleam。

senses.title: To appear briefly in the eyes
senses.definition: to show briefly in the eyes as a feeling or quality
senses.definitionCN: 作为情绪或品质在眼中短暂显现
senses.example: Amusement gleamed in his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 他眼中闪过一丝笑意。
senses.why: Emotions show as a passing light in the face, so the verb follows the eye sense.
senses.whyCN: 情绪会像掠过脸上的光一样显现，所以动词沿用了「眼中的光」这一义项。

intro.en: Gleam goes back to Old English glæm, a bright light, from a Germanic root for shining.
intro.cn: gleam 可追溯到古英语 glæm（明亮的光），源自日耳曼语中表示发光的词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root *ghel- carries the idea of shining and of gold.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ghel- 带有发光与黄金之意。

items.en: *glaimiz names brightness and a spark.
items.cn: *glaimiz 指明亮与火花。

items.en: Glæm means brightness, splendour, or a gleam of light.
items.cn: glæm 指明亮度、光辉或一线光。

items.en: Gleme keeps the noun and begins to name a brief flash.
items.cn: 中古英语 gleme 保留名词用法，并开始指短暂的闪光。

items.en: Gleam becomes both noun and verb and gains figurative uses.
items.cn: 现代英语中 gleam 兼作名词与动词，并获得比喻用法。

note.en: Gleam belongs to a Germanic light family with glimmer, and it sits near glint, glow, and shimmer.
note.cn: gleam 与 glimmer 同属日耳曼语的光亮词族，并与 glint、glow、shimmer 意义相邻。

normalIntro.en: Gleam is a slender light, often returned from a smooth surface.
normalIntro.cn: gleam 是一束细瘦的光，常常由光滑表面反射而来。

normal.en: A gleam of hope uses light as a metaphor for a small chance.
normal.cn: a gleam of hope 用光来比喻很小的机会。

normal.en: Gleam and glimmer both suggest a faint, unsteady light.
normal.cn: gleam 与 glimmer 都暗示微弱而不稳定的光。

normal.en: The verb gleam often pairs with wet, polished, or metallic surfaces.
normal.cn: 动词 gleam 常与潮湿、打磨过或金属的表面搭配。

normal.en: Gleaming is the participle and also an adjective meaning shining.
normal.cn: gleaming 是分词，也是表示「闪耀的」形容词。

normal.en: Old English glæm meant brightness and splendour, not a modern lamp.
normal.cn: 古英语 glæm 指明亮度与光辉，并非现代意义上的灯。

abstract.en: See a thin blade of light under a closed door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇关着的门下透出一条细光。

abstract.en: See a silver spoon catching a candle flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一把银勺接住烛火的亮光。

abstract.en: See one small spark at the end of a dark tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗隧道尽头的一点小火花。

examples.en: A gleam of light came through the gap under the door.
examples.cn: 一线微光从门下的缝隙透进来。

examples.en: The polished table gleamed in the afternoon sun.
examples.cn: 打磨过的桌子在午后阳光下泛着光。

examples.en: Hope gleamed in her eyes when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到消息时，她眼里闪出希望的光。

root: 原始日耳曼语 *glaimiz（光亮）→ 古英语 glæm（明亮、光辉）→ 中古英语 gleme → 英语 gleam，核心义「柔和而短暂的光」。

sensesIntro.en: Gleam starts as a soft light, becomes reflected shine and a trace of feeling, then turns into a verb for shining softly and for feelings that show in the eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: gleam 从柔和的光起步，延伸为反射的光泽与情绪的蛛丝马迹，再转化为表示发微光和情绪在眼中闪现的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin beam of light sliding across a dark surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束细光在黑暗的表面轻轻滑过。

branches.en: The plain light sense is the base.
branches.cn: 单纯的光是基础义项。

branches.en: Reflection is light returned by a surface.
branches.cn: 反射是表面送回来的光。

branches.en: Hope is the light metaphor carried into feeling.
branches.cn: 希望是光之比喻延伸到情感的结果。

branches.en: A gleam in the eye is a small light in a person.
branches.cn: 眼中的光是落在人身上的一小片亮光。

branches.en: Hope and amusement both appear as a brief gleam.
branches.cn: 希望与笑意都以短暂的一闪出现。

intro.en: Gleam is a Germanic word with a small English family: gleaming, gleamy, and the related glimmer.
intro.cn: gleam 是日耳曼语词，英语中有一个小词族：gleaming、gleamy，以及相关的 glimmer。

latinIntro.en: Gleam has no Latin source or cognate; Latin lux means light but is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: gleam 没有拉丁语来源或同源词；拉丁语 lux 意为光，但与之无关。

items.example: Gleam also works as a verb.

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 gleaming。

definition_zh: 使害怕；使惊恐；吓跑
definition_en: to make a person or animal feel fear or alarm
core_image: 黑暗中突然伸出的手，让人心口一紧并后退
scene: 深夜楼道里灯忽然灭了，一声响动把门口的小狗吓得跳起来。A sudden noise in the dark hallway frightened the little dog at the door.
sceneCN: 这里 frighten 是「使害怕」（第 1 个义项：让人或动物感到恐惧）；句意：黑暗楼道里突然的响动把门口的小狗吓了一大跳。

derivatives.zh: 由 frighten 加 -ed 构成，义为「害怕的；受惊的」
由 frighten 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人害怕的」
frighten 的名词来源，义为「突然的恐惧」
由 fright 加 -ful 构成，义为「可怕的；极度的」

senses.title: To make someone afraid
senses.definition: to make a person or animal feel fear
senses.definitionCN: 让人或动物感到恐惧
senses.example: The loud thunder frightened the children.
senses.exampleCN: 响亮的雷声吓到了孩子们。
senses.why: Fright names sudden fear, and the suffix -en turns it into the act of causing that fear.
senses.whyCN: fright 指突然的恐惧，后缀 -en 把名词变成「使人产生这种恐惧」的动作。

senses.title: To cause worry about something
senses.definition: to make someone feel worried or uneasy about a possible event
senses.definitionCN: 让人对可能发生的事感到担忧或不安
senses.example: The rising cost of housing frightens many young families.
senses.exampleCN: 不断上涨的住房成本让许多年轻家庭感到担忧。
senses.why: Fear can be directed at the future, not only at a present danger.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧不仅可以指向眼前的危险，也可以指向未来。

senses.title: To scare someone into or out of doing something
senses.titleCN: 吓得（某人）去做或不敢做
senses.definition: to force someone to act or stop acting by making them afraid
senses.definitionCN: 通过使人害怕来迫使其行动或停止行动
senses.example: They frightened him into signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他们吓得他签了合同。
senses.why: Fear is a tool of pressure, so the verb also means to drive someone by scaring them.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧是一种施压工具，所以这个动词也指用吓唬来驱使人。

senses.title: To drive away by fear
senses.definition: to make a person or animal leave by frightening them
senses.definitionCN: 通过惊吓让人或动物离开
senses.example: The farmer frightened the crows away from the corn.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把乌鸦从玉米地吓跑了。
senses.why: When the frightened creature runs, the verb takes on the sense of driving it off.
senses.whyCN: 受惊的生物会跑开，于是这个动词获得了「把其赶走」的含义。

senses.title: To startle an animal
senses.definition: to startle an animal so that it moves suddenly or bolts
senses.definitionCN: 使动物受惊，从而突然移动或狂奔
senses.example: The flash of the camera frightened the horse.
senses.exampleCN: 相机的闪光让马受了惊。
senses.why: Animals react to fear with sudden movement, and the word describes the trigger.
senses.whyCN: 动物面对恐惧会突然行动，这个词就描述引发反应的那个刺激。

senses.title: To give someone a sudden shock
senses.definition: to give someone a sudden shock or alarm
senses.definitionCN: 给人突然的惊吓或震动
senses.example: The scream in the night frightened everyone in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里的尖叫把屋里所有人都吓了一跳。
senses.why: Sudden fear is the oldest sense, and a shock is fear arriving all at once.
senses.whyCN: 突然的恐惧是最早的含义，而惊吓就是恐惧一下子袭来。

intro.en: Frighten is an English verb built from the noun fright, which comes from Old English fyrhto, fear.
intro.cn: frighten 是由名词 fright 构成的英语动词，而 fright 来自古英语 fyrhto（恐惧）。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *furhtō means fear.
items.cn: 重构名词 *furhtō 意为恐惧。

items.en: Fyrhto and fyrhtu name fear and dread.
items.cn: fyrhto 与 fyrhtu 指恐惧与畏惧。

items.en: Fright names sudden fear, and the verb is built on it.
items.cn: 中古英语 fright 指突然的恐惧，动词由它构成。

items.en: Frighten appears as the verb formed with -en.
items.cn: frighten 作为加 -en 构成的动词出现。

items.en: Frighten spreads into phrasal uses such as frighten away and frighten into.
items.cn: frighten 扩展到 frighten away、frighten into 等短语用法。

note.en: Frighten is the verb of the fright family, and it sits near scare, alarm, and terrify.
note.cn: frighten 是 fright 词族的动词，并与 scare、alarm、terrify 意义相邻。

sensesIntro.en: Frighten begins with the act of causing fear, extends to worry about the future, to pressure through fear, to driving away, to startling animals, and finally to a sudden shock.
sensesIntro.cn: frighten 从「使人恐惧」这一动作出发，延伸到对未来的担忧、以恐惧施压、把对象赶走、使动物受惊，最后指突然的惊吓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sudden dark shape that makes the body pull back.
core.cn: 核心意象：突然出现的黑影让身体往后一缩。

branches.en: Making someone afraid is the core sense.
branches.cn: 使人害怕是核心义项。

branches.en: Worry about the future extends fear forward in time.
branches.cn: 对未来的担忧把恐惧延伸到以后。

branches.en: Fear used as pressure forces a decision.
branches.cn: 被当作压力的恐惧会迫使对象做出决定。

branches.en: Driving away is fear turned into movement.
branches.cn: 赶走是恐惧转化为动作的结果。

branches.en: Animals and people both startle when fear strikes.
branches.cn: 恐惧袭来时，动物和人都会受惊。

definition_zh: 令人害怕的；可怕的；惊人的
definition_en: causing fear, alarm, or worry
core_image: 门后传来低沉的撞击声，屋里的人不敢出声
scene: 夜里有人敲门却不说自己是谁，屋内的沉默持续了很久。Someone knocked at night without saying who they were, and the silence inside was frightening.
sceneCN: 这里 frightening 是「令人害怕的」（第 1 个义项：引起恐惧的）；句意：夜里有人敲门却不说自己是谁，屋里的沉默令人害怕。

pos.zh: 令人害怕的；可怕的；惊人的

frightening 的动词来源，义为「使害怕」
词族中的名词，义为「突然的恐惧」

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: making someone feel fear
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恐惧的
senses.example: The film contains several frightening scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影里有几场令人害怕的戏。
senses.why: The present participle of frighten describes whatever produces the fear.
senses.whyCN: frighten 的现在分词用来描述引起恐惧的事物。

senses.title: Causing worry about the future
senses.definition: making people feel anxious about what may happen
senses.definitionCN: 让人对可能发生的事感到焦虑的
senses.example: The report paints a frightening picture of the next decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为未来十年描绘了一幅令人担忧的图景。
senses.why: Fear pointed at the future becomes worry, and the adjective follows it.
senses.whyCN: 指向未来的恐惧会变成担忧，这个形容词也随之扩展到担忧。

senses.title: Alarmingly large or fast
senses.titleCN: 大得惊人的；快得吓人的
senses.definition: used of numbers, rates, or changes that are alarmingly great
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容大得令人警觉的数字、比率或变化
senses.example: The disease spread at a frightening rate.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病以惊人的速度传播。
senses.why: A rate that is large enough to scare people is described as frightening.
senses.whyCN: 大到足以让人害怕的速率，就被形容为 frightening。

senses.title: Very bad or serious
senses.definition: extremely bad, serious, or difficult to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 极其糟糕、严重或难以应对的
senses.example: The team was in a frightening position near the bottom of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队处在积分榜末尾附近，处境糟得可怕。
senses.why: When a situation is bad enough to cause fear, the adjective names the whole situation.
senses.whyCN: 当局面糟到足以引起恐惧时，这个形容词就用来形容整个局面。

senses.title: Seeming threatening
senses.definition: looking or sounding likely to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 外表或声音显得可能造成伤害的
senses.example: The mask gave him a frightening appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 那副面具让他看上去很吓人。
senses.why: A threatening look is a promise of fear, and the adjective names that promise.
senses.whyCN: 带有威胁的外表预示着恐惧，这个形容词就指这种预示。

senses.title: So impressive that it almost frightens
senses.definition: so impressive or intense that it feels almost frightening
senses.definitionCN: 令人印象深刻或强烈到近乎骇人的
senses.example: She has a frightening command of the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这门学科的掌握程度令人敬畏。
senses.why: Awe and fear are neighbours, so great skill can be called frightening.
senses.whyCN: 敬畏与恐惧是近邻，所以高超的能力也可以被称为 frightening。

intro.en: Frightening is the present participle of frighten, used as an adjective for whatever causes fear.
intro.cn: frightening 是 frighten 的现在分词，用作形容词，指引起恐惧的事物。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *furhtō means fear.
items.cn: 重构名词 *furhtō 意为恐惧。

items.en: Fyrhto names fear and dread.
items.cn: fyrhto 指恐惧与畏惧。

items.en: Fright names sudden fear.
items.cn: 中古英语 fright 指突然的恐惧。

items.en: Frighten appears as a verb formed with -en.
items.cn: frighten 作为加 -en 构成的动词出现。

items.en: Frightening settles as an adjective for events, prospects, and rates.
items.cn: frightening 固定为形容事件、前景与速率的形容词。

note.en: Frightening is the adjective of the fright family, and it sits near scary, alarming, and terrifying.
note.cn: frightening 是 fright 词族的形容词，并与 scary、alarming、terrifying 意义相邻。

entries.definition: to make someone afraid
feeling fear
causing fear; very bad
causing fear
causing worry or fear
entries.definitionCN: 令人警觉的；使人担忧的

entries.definition: extremely frightening

normalIntro.en: Frightening is the active participle: it is the thing that gives fear, not the person who feels it.
normalIntro.cn: frightening 是主动分词：它指带来恐惧的事物，而不是感到恐惧的人。

normal.en: Frightening describes the cause; frightened describes the person: a frightening dog and a frightened child.
normal.cn: frightening 描述原因，frightened 描述人：a frightening dog 与 a frightened child。

normal.en: Frightening is built from frighten plus -ing, like alarming from alarm.
normal.cn: frightening 由 frighten 加 -ing 构成，就像 alarming 由 alarm 构成。

normal.en: A frightening rate is a rate so high that it alarms people.
normal.cn: a frightening rate 指高到让人警觉的速率。

normal.en: Frighteningly is the adverb: prices rose frighteningly fast.
normal.cn: frighteningly 是副词：prices rose frighteningly fast。

normal.en: Frightful is a near cousin, also meaning causing fear.
normal.cn: frightful 是近亲词，也表示引起恐惧。

abstract.en: See a dark door with a low knock behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇黑门，门后传来低沉的敲击声。

abstract.en: See a chart line climbing off the page.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的一条线一路爬出纸面。

abstract.en: See a wall of water moving faster than people can run.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵水墙移动得比人跑得还快。

examples.en: The storm produced a frightening wall of water.
examples.cn: 风暴掀起了一堵可怕的水墙。

examples.en: It is frightening how quickly the fire spread.
examples.cn: 火势蔓延之快令人害怕。

examples.en: The most frightening part was the silence that followed.
examples.cn: 最可怕的是随后而来的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗莱特宁」——读音近似「frightening」，可联想「发抖加上拧紧」：把人吓得心都拧起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: frighten（使害怕）+ 现在分词后缀 -ing → frightening，核心义「持续散发令人害怕之感的」。

sensesIntro.en: Frightening begins with whatever causes fear, then extends to worry about the future, to alarmingly large figures, to a bad situation, to a threatening look, and finally to awe.
sensesIntro.cn: frightening 先从引起恐惧的事物出发，再指对未来的担忧、大得惊人的数字、糟糕的处境、带有威胁的外表，最后指令人敬畏的气势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knock behind a closed door that keeps everyone silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：关着的门后传来敲击声，让所有人不敢出声。

branches.en: Causing fear is the base sense.
branches.cn: 引起恐惧是基础义项。

branches.en: Worry about the future is fear moved forward.
branches.cn: 对未来的担忧是把恐惧推向前方。

branches.en: Fear and alarmingly great size share one adjective.
branches.cn: 恐惧与大得惊人的规模共用同一个形容词。

branches.en: A bad position and a threatening look both alarm people.
branches.cn: 糟糕的处境与吓人的外表都会让人警觉。

branches.en: Awe is the far end of the same scale.
branches.cn: 敬畏是同一条尺度上最远的一端。

intro.en: Frightening is an English participle adjective from frighten, itself fright plus -en, with frighteningly and frightful nearby.
intro.cn: frightening 是由 frighten 构成的英语分词形容词，而 frighten 是 fright 加 -en，附近还有 frighteningly 与 frightful。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate; Latin timor means fear but is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语同源词；拉丁语 timor 意为恐惧，但两者无关。

items.example: Fyrhto is the Old English noun for fear.
items.exampleCN: fyrhto 是古英语中表示恐惧的名词。

items.example: Fright names sudden fear in Middle English.
items.exampleCN: fright 在中古英语中表示突然的恐惧。

items.example: Fright is the noun in this family.
items.exampleCN: fright 是这个词族里的名词。

items.example: Frighten adds -en to fright.
items.exampleCN: frighten 是在 fright 后加 -en。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词与形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing turns frighten into frightening.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 把 frighten 变成 frightening。

items.example: Frightening works as both participle and adjective.
items.exampleCN: frightening 既是分词也是形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms frighteningly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 frighteningly。

items.example: Frightful comes from fright plus -ful.
items.exampleCN: frightful 来自 fright 加 -ful。

items.example: Frightened describes the person who feels fear.
items.exampleCN: frightened 描述感到恐惧的人。

definition_zh: 寒冷；严寒；冷淡；冷漠；性冷淡
definition_en: the quality of being very cold, or a lack of warmth in manner, feeling, or physical response
core_image: 结霜的玻璃：外面白茫茫，里面的人仍觉得冷
scene: 冬天的清晨，窗玻璃上结满冰花，屋里的人裹紧毯子。The frigidity of the mountain air turned every breath into a white cloud.
sceneCN: 这里 frigidity 是「严寒」（第 1 个义项：极低的温度）；句意：山间空气的严寒让每一次呼吸都变成一团白雾。

pos.zh: 寒冷；严寒；冷淡；冷漠；性冷淡

derivatives.zh: 寒冷的；冷淡的
冷淡地；冰冷地
寒冷；冷淡（由 frigid 加 -ness 构成）
致冷的；产生寒意的

senses.title: Extreme cold
senses.definition: the state or quality of being extremely cold in temperature
senses.definitionCN: 温度极低的状态或性质
senses.example: The frigidity of the polar night froze the fuel in its pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 极夜的严寒把管道里的燃料冻住了。
senses.why: The Latin noun frigiditas names coldness itself, so the first sense is plain temperature.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 frigiditas 本义就是「寒冷」，所以第一个义项直接指温度的低。

senses.title: A bodily sense of cold
senses.definition: the cold sensation given by air, water, or a hard surface
senses.definitionCN: 空气、水或坚硬表面带来的寒冷感觉
senses.example: She drew back from the frigidity of the lake water.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水冰冷，她缩了回去。
senses.why: Coldness felt on the skin is the same Latin quality seen from the body, so the noun can name a sensation rather than a reading.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤感到的冷仍是同一种拉丁语「冷」，只是从身体感受去看，于是这个名词也能指一种感觉而非温度读数。

senses.title: Coldness of manner
senses.definition: a reserved and unfriendly way of behaving that shows no warmth
senses.definitionCN: 矜持而不友好的举止，不显热情
senses.example: The frigidity of the old butler made visitors uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 老管家的冷淡让访客感到不安。
senses.why: A cold temperature becomes a cold heart: the physical image of frost transfers to social behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 低温变成冷心肠：霜的物理画面被移到社交举止上。

senses.title: Lack of enthusiasm
senses.definition: an absence of interest or excitement about an activity or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动或想法缺少兴趣与兴奋
senses.example: The frigidity of the audience ended the concert early.
senses.exampleCN: 观众的冷淡让音乐会提前结束。
senses.why: Warmth also means eagerness, so a lack of warmth can name a lack of eager interest.
senses.whyCN: 「暖」也意味着热切，因此缺少暖意可以指缺少热切的兴趣。

senses.title: Sexual unresponsiveness
senses.definition: a clinical term for a lack of sexual desire or response
senses.definitionCN: 临床用语，指缺乏性欲或性反应
senses.example: Clinics once listed frigidity as a disorder of women only.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所曾把性冷淡只列为女性的障碍。
senses.why: Medical Latin took the cold metaphor into the body and used it for a cold sexual temperament.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语把这套「冷」的比喻带进身体，用来指性方面的冷性气质。

senses.title: Coldness of style
senses.definition: a style or artistic manner that avoids warmth, emotion, and ornament
senses.definitionCN: 回避热情、情感与装饰的风格或艺术手法
senses.example: Critics spoke of the frigidity of the prose in that novel.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家谈到那部小说散文的冷峻。
senses.why: Style can be warm or cold, so the same noun judges writing that refuses feeling.
senses.whyCN: 风格有暖有冷，于是同一个名词也用来评判拒绝情感的文字。

senses.title: Cold constitution in old medicine
senses.definition: in older medicine, a cold temperament or constitution of the body
senses.definitionCN: 旧时医学中指身体偏寒的体质或气质
senses.example: Physicians blamed slow digestion on a frigidity of the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把消化缓慢归咎于体质的寒性。
senses.why: Before thermometers, cold was a humour of the body, and frigidity named a bodily mixture.
senses.whyCN: 在温度计出现之前，「冷」是身体的一种体液性质，frigidity 指的正是身体的寒性配比。

senses.title: Frozen distance between people
senses.definition: a strained and unfriendly state of relations between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间或群体之间紧张而不友好的关系状态
senses.example: The frigidity between the two families lasted for a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人之间的僵冷持续了一代人的时间。
senses.why: Coldness between people hardens into a frozen distance, which the noun can describe as a state of relations.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的冷意凝固成冰冻的距离，这个名词便用来描述这种关系状态。

intro.en: Frigidity comes from Latin frigiditas, coldness, built on frigidus, cold, from frigere, to be cold.
intro.cn: frigidity 来自拉丁语 frigiditas（寒冷），由 frigidus（冷的）构成，源于 frigere（变冷）。

items.en: A root for cold lies behind the family, and Greek rhigos, frost, is usually taken as a cognate.
items.cn: 这个词族的远源是一个表示「冷」的词根；一般认为希腊语 rhigos（霜）与它同源。

items.en: Frigus means cold, and frigere means to be cold.
items.cn: frigus 意为寒冷，frigere 意为变冷、发冷。

items.en: Frigidus, cold, yields the noun frigiditas, coldness.
items.cn: frigidus（冷的）构成名词 frigiditas（寒冷）。

items.en: Medical Latin uses frigiditas for a cold constitution of the body.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 frigiditas 指身体的寒性体质。

items.en: English borrows frigidity as a learned word for coldness.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 frigidity，作为表达「寒冷」的书卷词。

items.en: Modern medicine and psychology add the sexual sense to the old word.
items.cn: 现代医学与心理学给这个旧词添上性方面的义项。

note.en: Frigidity belongs to the Latin cold family of frigid, frigidly, and frigidness, and stands near ordinary cold words.
note.cn: frigidity 属于拉丁语「冷」词族，与 frigid、frigidly、frigidness 同根，并与普通的「冷」义词相邻。

entries.definition: very cold; lacking warmth
in a cold or distant way
the quality of being cold
a lack of heat or of friendly feeling
a cold feeling in the air or in a manner
