normalIntro.en: Frigidity is the noun of frigid, and the cold it names runs from weather to manners to medicine.
normalIntro.cn: frigidity 是 frigid 的名词形式，它所名的「冷」从天气一路走到态度与医学。

normal.en: Frigid is the adjective, and -ity turns it into the noun frigidity.
normal.cn: frigid 是形容词，加上 -ity 就成了名词 frigidity。

normal.en: The Latin root frigus, cold, also hides inside refrigerate.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 frigus（寒冷）也藏在 refrigerate（冷藏）里面。

normal.en: Sexual frigidity is the clinical sense, and it belongs to medical Latin.
normal.cn: sexual frigidity 是临床义项，来自医学拉丁语。

normal.en: A frigidity of manner is the same as an icy distance between people.
normal.cn: a frigidity of manner 就等于人与人之间冰冷的距离。

normal.en: Frigidity of style describes writing that refuses warmth and ornament.
normal.cn: frigidity of style 形容拒绝热情与装饰的文字。

abstract.en: See a frosted window with the lamp burning inside and no heat reaching the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇结霜的窗，屋里灯亮着，却没有任何热量传到玻璃上。

abstract.en: Feel your hand enter cold lake water and withdraw at once.
abstract.cn: 想象手伸进冰冷的湖水，立刻缩了回来。

abstract.en: Watch a host greet guests with a stiff nod and no smile.
abstract.cn: 想象主人只点头招呼客人，脸上没有一丝笑容。

examples.en: The frigidity of the cellar kept the apples crisp all winter.
examples.cn: 地窖的寒冷让苹果整个冬天都保持脆硬。

examples.en: His frigidity toward new neighbours was read as pride.
examples.cn: 他对新邻居的冷淡被解读为骄傲。

examples.en: Doctors no longer treat frigidity as a disorder of women.
examples.cn: 医生不再把性冷淡当作女性特有的障碍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞吉迪提」——开头像 freezing（结冰），中间像「急」，冷得人直打哆嗦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 frigus（寒冷）与 frigere（变冷）→ frigidus（冷的）→ 晚期拉丁语 frigiditas（寒冷；寒性体质）→ 英语 frigidity；核心义始终是「冷」，再由身体温度延伸到态度与情感。

sensesIntro.en: Frigidity begins as the plain cold of air and water, then passes to cold manners, to missing interest, to clinical coldness, to cold style, to old medicine, and to frozen relations.
sensesIntro.cn: frigidity 先指空气与水的实际低温，再依次指冷淡的举止、缺失的兴趣、临床的性冷淡、冷峻的文风、旧医学的寒性体质，最后指僵冷的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frosted pane of glass that lets light through but keeps warmth out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇结霜的玻璃，透得过光，透不过暖。

branches.en: Physical cold and the chill it gives are the literal base.
branches.cn: 物理的冷与它带来的寒感是字面基础。

branches.en: Cold manners and missing interest are the social branch.
branches.cn: 冷淡的举止与缺失的兴趣是社交分支。

branches.en: Clinical coldness is the medical branch.
branches.cn: 临床的性冷淡是医学分支。

branches.en: Style and old medicine both borrow the temperature image.
branches.cn: 文风与旧医学都借用了温度意象。

branches.en: Relations can freeze into a lasting distance.
branches.cn: 人际关系会冻结成持久的距离。

intro.en: Frigidity is built on the Latin cold family of frigus, frigere, and frigidus, with English frigid and frigidly around it.
intro.cn: frigidity 建立在拉丁语「冷」词族 frigus、frigere、frigidus 之上，周围有英语 frigid 与 frigidly。

latinIntro.en: Latin frigus is cold, frigere is to be cold, and frigiditas is the noun of coldness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frigus 是寒冷，frigere 是变冷，frigiditas 是表示寒冷的名词。

items.example: Frigus gives the family its cold image.
items.exampleCN: frigus 给这个词族提供了「冷」的意象。

items.example: Frigere supplies the verb idea of being cold.
items.exampleCN: frigere 提供「处于寒冷」的动词概念。

items.example: Frigidus is the adjective behind frigid.
items.exampleCN: frigidus 是 frigid 背后的形容词。

items.example: Frigiditas is the direct source of frigidity.
items.exampleCN: frigiditas 是 frigidity 的直接来源。

items.example: French frigidité keeps the learned tone.
items.exampleCN: 法语 frigidité 保留了书卷语气。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity turns frigid into frigidity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把 frigid 变成 frigidity。

items.example: Frigid describes air or a manner.
items.exampleCN: frigid 形容空气或态度。

items.example: Frigidity names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: frigidity 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Frigidly answers how someone spoke.
items.exampleCN: frigidly 说明某人说话的方式。

items.example: Frigorific belongs to the technical cold family.
items.exampleCN: frigorific 属于技术性的「冷」词族。

definition_zh: 结霜的；霜寒的；冰冷的；冷淡的；冷遇的
definition_en: covered with frost, very cold, or showing no warmth of manner
core_image: 草叶上覆着一层白霜，脚一踩就碎
scene: 清早的草地一片白，呼出的气在空气里散成雾。The frosty grass crunched under their boots as they crossed the field.
sceneCN: 这里 frosty 是「结霜的」（第 1 个义项：表面覆着一层白霜）；句意：结霜的草地在他们靴子下踩出脆响，他们正穿过田野。

derivatives.zh: 霜；结霜
冷淡地；冰冷地
霜寒；冷淡
结霜的；磨砂的
除霜；解冻

senses.title: Covered with frost
senses.definition: covered with a thin white layer of frost
senses.definitionCN: 表面覆着一层薄薄的白霜
senses.example: The frosty lawn sparkled in the early light.
senses.exampleCN: 结霜的草坪在晨光里闪闪发亮。
senses.why: Frost is frozen dew on a clear cold night, and the adjective simply says that this frost is present.
senses.whyCN: 霜是晴冷夜里冻住的露水，这个形容词只是说这层霜就在那儿。

senses.title: Cold enough for frost
senses.definition: very cold, of the kind of weather that produces frost
senses.definitionCN: 冷到能结霜的；严寒的
senses.example: A frosty wind cut through the market square.
senses.exampleCN: 霜寒的风穿过集市广场。
senses.why: If frost forms, the air is below freezing, so frosty moves from the white deposit to the weather that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 霜一结成，气温就在冰点以下，于是 frosty 从白色的霜转到造出霜的天气。

senses.title: Piercingly cold to the skin
senses.definition: unpleasantly cold to the touch or on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 触感或体感令人不适的冷
senses.example: The frosty metal of the gate stung her palm.
senses.exampleCN: 铁门冰冷的金属刺痛了她的手心。
senses.why: Anything as cold as frost feels sharp, so frosty can describe a surface that bites the hand.
senses.whyCN: 凡是冷得像霜的东西，摸上去都带刺感，所以 frosty 也能形容咬手的表面。

senses.title: Cold in manner
senses.definition: distant and unfriendly in behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 举止疏远而不友好
senses.example: He gave a frosty nod and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他冷淡地点了下头，什么也没说。
senses.why: A cold surface becomes a cold person: the white crust of frost turns into visible reserve.
senses.whyCN: 冷的表面变成冷的人：那层白霜化作看得见的疏远。

senses.title: Hostile in welcome or response
senses.definition: unwelcoming or disapproving, of a reception or a reply
senses.definitionCN: 接待或回应不热情、带否定意味
senses.example: The plan met a frosty response from the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划遭到委员会冷淡的回应。
senses.why: A reception can be warm or frosty, so the weather word judges how a group receives an idea.
senses.whyCN: 接待可以是暖的，也可以是霜冷的，于是天气词用来评判一个群体如何接受某个想法。

senses.title: A smile without warmth
senses.definition: a smile that shows politeness but no warmth
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌却不带暖意的笑
senses.example: She answered with a frosty smile that ended the talk.
senses.exampleCN: 她用冷淡的一笑作答，谈话就此结束。
senses.why: A face can carry frost too, and a frosty smile is the polite mask of a cold feeling.
senses.whyCN: 脸上也能挂霜，冷淡的笑就是冷意外面那层礼貌的面具。

senses.title: White like frost
senses.definition: white or grey-white in colour, as if covered with frost
senses.definitionCN: 颜色白或灰白，像覆着一层霜
senses.example: Frosty hair framed the face of the old sailor.
senses.exampleCN: 霜白的头发衬着老水手的面庞。
senses.why: Frost is white, so the adjective can name any pale, silvery whiteness that looks like rime.
senses.whyCN: 霜是白的，于是这个形容词可以指任何像雾凇一样的浅淡银白。

senses.title: Covered with a frost-like mist
senses.definition: covered with a thin white mist or condensation, as a pane of glass
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃等表面蒙着一层白色水汽或冷凝物
senses.example: The frosty window hid the street from view.
senses.exampleCN: 蒙着霜雾的窗把街道遮住了。
senses.why: Cold glass collects a white film that looks like frost, so the word also names that frosted surface.
senses.whyCN: 冰冷的玻璃会积起一层像霜的白膜，于是这个词也用来指那种起霜的表面。

intro.en: Frosty is frost plus the adjective suffix -y, and frost goes back to a Germanic verb meaning to freeze.
intro.cn: frosty 是 frost 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，而 frost 可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「冻结」的动词。

items.en: The reconstructed root preus- carries both freezing and the burning sensation of cold.
items.cn: 重构词根 preus- 同时带有「冻结」与「冷得灼人」的意思。

items.en: Freusan gives the verb to freeze, and frustaz gives the noun frost.
items.cn: freusan 是「冻结」的动词，frustaz 是「霜」的名词。

items.en: Frost names the frozen dew of a clear winter night.
items.cn: 古英语 frost 指晴冷冬夜里冻住的露水。

items.en: The adjective frosty is formed from frost by adding the suffix -y.
items.cn: 中古英语用 frost 加后缀 -y 构成形容词 frosty。

items.en: Early records of frosty describe weather, ground, and grass.
items.cn: frosty 的早期记录描述天气、地面与草叶。

items.en: Modern English extends frosty to smiles, welcomes, colour, and glass.
items.cn: 现代英语把 frosty 扩展到笑容、接待、颜色与玻璃。

note.en: Frosty is the adjective of frost, standing close to frostily and frostiness, and near the wider family of cold words.
note.cn: frosty 是 frost 的形容词，与 frostily、frostiness 同族，并与更广的「冷」义词相邻。

entries.definition: a thin white layer of frozen dew
entries.definitionCN: 冻结的露水形成的薄薄白层

entries.definition: in a cold or unfriendly way
the quality of being frosty
covered with ice or very cold
cold in a mild or unpleasant way
belonging to winter and therefore cold

normalIntro.en: Frosty is frost made into an adjective, and its meanings follow the white crust from the ground to the face.
normalIntro.cn: frosty 是把 frost 变成形容词，它的义项跟着那层白霜从地面走到人的脸上。

normal.en: Frost is the noun, and the suffix -y says that frost is present.
normal.cn: frost 是名词，后缀 -y 表示「带着霜」。

normal.en: Frost, freeze, and frosty share one Germanic family.
normal.cn: frost、freeze 与 frosty 同属一个日耳曼词族。

normal.en: A frosty morning is a morning cold enough to leave frost.
normal.cn: a frosty morning 就是冷得能留下霜的早晨。

normal.en: A frosty reception is a welcome as warm as a frozen step.
normal.cn: a frosty reception 就是冷得像冰冻台阶一样的接待。

normal.en: Frosted glass and a frosty window both carry that white film.
normal.cn: frosted glass 与 frosty window 都带着那层白色薄膜。

abstract.en: Picture white grass crunching under a boot at sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象日出时白色的草地，靴子一踩就发出脆响。

abstract.en: Feel the wind that makes your breath visible.
abstract.cn: 想象那种让你呼出的气变成白雾的风。

abstract.en: Touch a frozen gate and feel the sting on your palm.
abstract.cn: 想象摸到冰冷的铁门，手心被刺得一缩。

examples.en: The path was frosty and slippery before sunrise.
examples.cn: 日出前小路结着霜，又滑又脆。

examples.en: Her frosty reply made it clear that the offer was refused.
examples.cn: 她冷淡的回答表明那个提议已被拒绝。

examples.en: He scraped the frosty windscreen with an old card.
examples.cn: 他用一张旧卡片刮掉挡风玻璃上的霜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗罗斯提」——听起来就是 frost（霜）加上 -y，又冷又脆；这只是谐音与拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 frost（霜）加形容词后缀 -y → frosty；更早可追溯到原始日耳曼语 freusan（冻结）与原始印欧语重构词根 preus-（冻、冷）。

sensesIntro.en: Frosty starts with frost on the ground, moves to the cold that creates it, then to cold surfaces, cold manners, cold welcomes, cold smiles, frost-white colour, and frosted glass.
sensesIntro.cn: frosty 从地上的霜开始，转到造霜的严寒，再到冰冷的表面、冷淡的举止、冷遇、冷淡的笑、霜白的颜色与起霜的玻璃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white crust of frost on grass at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时草地上薄薄一层白霜。

branches.en: Frost on the ground and the weather that makes it are the literal pair.
branches.cn: 地上的霜与造出霜的天气是字面的一对。

branches.en: A surface as cold as frost gives the touch sense.
branches.cn: 冷得像霜的表面给出触感义项。

branches.en: Reserve of manner and a cold smile are the personal branch.
branches.cn: 疏远的举止与冷淡的笑是人的分支。

branches.en: A frosty reception judges how a group answers an idea.
branches.cn: 冷遇用来评判一个群体如何回应某个想法。

branches.en: Frost-white colour and frosted glass keep the visual image.
branches.cn: 霜白的颜色与起霜的玻璃保留了视觉意象。

intro.en: Frosty is frost plus the adjective suffix -y, a Germanic word with English relatives such as frost, frostily, and defrost.
intro.cn: frosty 是 frost 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，属于日耳曼语词，英语同族词有 frost、frostily 与 defrost。

latinIntro.en: Frosty is Germanic in origin and has no direct Latin source word, so no Latin source entries are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: frosty 源自日耳曼语，没有直接的拉丁语来源词，因此这里不列拉丁语来源条目。

items.exampleCN: frosty 形容地面、空气与态度。

items.example: Frostily describes how a reply is given.
items.exampleCN: frostily 描述回话的方式。

items.example: Frostiness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: frostiness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: Frosted glass keeps the same white film.
items.exampleCN: frosted glass 保留同样的白色薄膜。

items.example: Defrost adds the prefix de- to frost.
items.exampleCN: defrost 是 frost 加上前缀 de-。

definition_zh: 冰冻的；冷冻的；冻僵的；封冻的；冻结的
definition_en: turned into ice, preserved by cold, numb with cold, or fixed and unable to move or change
core_image: 整片湖面冻成一块灰白的冰
scene: 寒夜里湖面冻成一片灰白，孩子们试探着在冰上走。The frozen lake cracked under the weight of the sledge.
sceneCN: 这里 frozen 是「封冻的」（第 4 个义项：被冰覆盖或封住）；句意：冰封的湖面在雪橇的重量下裂开。

pos.zh: 冰冻的；冷冻的；冻僵的；冻结的

derivatives.zh: 冻结；冻住；僵住
冷冻柜；冰柜
极冷的；冰冻的
未冻结的；解冻的

senses.title: Turned into ice
senses.definition: changed from liquid to solid ice by cold
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷由液体变成固体的冰
senses.example: The pond is frozen solid from December to March.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘从十二月到三月都冻得硬实。
senses.why: Freeze comes from a Germanic verb for freezing, and its participle frozen names whatever the cold has turned to ice.
senses.whyCN: freeze 来自日耳曼语中表示「冻结」的动词，它的分词 frozen 指被寒冷变成冰的东西。

senses.title: Preserved by freezing
senses.definition: kept fresh by being stored at a very low temperature
senses.definitionCN: 用极低温度保存以保持新鲜
senses.example: She kept frozen peas in the bottom drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把冷冻豌豆放在最下面的抽屉里。
senses.why: Once ice stops food from spoiling, the participle becomes a label for food kept that way.
senses.whyCN: 冰能阻止食物变坏，于是这个分词就成了用这种方式保存的食品的标签。

senses.title: Numb or killed by cold
senses.definition: so cold that the body loses feeling or life
senses.definitionCN: 冷到身体失去知觉或生命
senses.example: His fingers were frozen after an hour in the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 在雪里待了一小时后，他的手指冻僵了。
senses.why: Living tissue chilled to ice loses feeling, so frozen passes from water to flesh.
senses.whyCN: 活的组织冷到结冰就失去知觉，于是 frozen 从水转到血肉之躯。

senses.title: Blocked or covered by ice
senses.definition: covered with ice or made impassable by ice
senses.definitionCN: 被冰覆盖或因冰而无法通行
senses.example: The frozen road stayed shut for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 封冻的道路封闭了三天。
senses.why: A sheet of ice over a surface closes it, so the participle can describe a route or a region sealed by cold.
senses.whyCN: 一层冰盖住表面就把路封住，于是这个分词可以形容被寒冷封死的路线或区域。

senses.title: Paralysed by fear or shock
senses.definition: unable to move because of fear, surprise, or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、惊讶或震惊而无法动弹
senses.example: She stood frozen when the door opened.
senses.exampleCN: 门开时她僵在原地。
senses.why: The body that cannot move feels as stiff as ice, so frozen describes fear that stops a person.
senses.whyCN: 动不了的身体硬得像冰，于是 frozen 形容把人定住的恐惧。

senses.title: Fixed and not allowed to change
senses.definition: held at a fixed level and not permitted to change
senses.definitionCN: 固定在某一水平、不允许变动
senses.example: The union accepted a frozen wage for one year.
senses.exampleCN: 工会接受了一年冻结的工资。
senses.why: Money and rules can be frozen like water, fixed in place so that nothing moves.
senses.whyCN: 钱与规则可以像水一样被冻住，固定原地，什么都不再流动。

senses.title: Showing no warmth
senses.definition: showing no feeling or warmth, of a face or a smile
senses.definitionCN: 脸上或笑容里没有情感与暖意
senses.example: He watched the scene with a frozen expression.
senses.exampleCN: 他面无表情地看着这一幕。
senses.why: A face without expression is stiff and cold, so the ice image returns as social distance.
senses.whyCN: 没有表情的脸又僵又冷，于是冰的意象又作为社交距离回来了。

senses.title: Unresponsive, of a device or program
senses.definition: stuck and not responding to commands, of a screen or a program
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕或程序卡住、不响应操作
senses.example: The frozen screen had to be restarted.
senses.exampleCN: 卡死的屏幕只能重启。
senses.why: A machine that stops moving looks frozen like ice, which gives the modern computing sense.
senses.whyCN: 停住不动的机器看起来像冻住的冰，这就生出计算机用语中的现代义项。

intro.en: Frozen is the past participle of freeze, from Old English freosan, from a Germanic verb for freezing.
intro.cn: frozen 是 freeze 的过去分词，源自古英语 freosan，再往前是日耳曼语中表示「冻结」的动词。

items.en: The reconstructed root preus- joins freezing with the burning feeling of extreme cold.
items.cn: 重构词根 preus- 把「冻结」与极冷时的灼痛感连在一起。

items.en: Freusan means to freeze, and its participle supplies the shape of frozen.
items.cn: freusan 意为冻结，它的分词提供 frozen 的形状。

items.en: Freosan is the Old English verb for freezing.
items.cn: freosan 是古英语中表示「冻结」的动词。

items.en: Frozen settles as the past participle while froze serves as the past tense.
items.cn: 中古英语里 frozen 固定为过去分词，froze 则作过去式。

items.en: Frozen begins to work as an adjective for water, roads, and food.
items.cn: 近代早期英语里 frozen 开始作形容词，形容水面、道路与食物。

items.en: Modern English applies frozen to assets, faces, and software.
items.cn: 现代英语把 frozen 用到资产、表情与软件上。

note.en: Frozen is the participle of freeze and stands beside froze and freezing, while the wider field includes icy, chilled, and frigid.
note.cn: frozen 是 freeze 的分词，与 froze、freezing 并列，更宽的义场里还有 icy、chilled 与 frigid。

the past tense of freeze
extremely cold; the act of turning to ice
covered with ice or extremely cold
made cold, often for storage
very cold; without warmth of feeling

normalIntro.en: Frozen is what freeze has already done, so every sense describes something that ice or cold has stopped.
normalIntro.cn: frozen 是 freeze 已经做完的结果，所以每个义项都描述被冰或寒冷停住的东西。

normal.en: Frozen is the past participle of freeze, so it names what the cold has done.
normal.cn: frozen 是 freeze 的过去分词，因此它指寒冷已经做成的事。

normal.en: Freeze, froze, and frozen follow the pattern of speak, spoke, and spoken.
normal.cn: freeze、froze、frozen 的变化跟 speak、spoke、spoken 一样。

normal.en: Frozen food and frozen assets both stay exactly as they were.
normal.cn: frozen food 与 frozen assets 都是保持原样、不再变化。

normal.en: A frozen smile is a face that will not move.
normal.cn: a frozen smile 就是一张不肯动的脸。

normal.en: Compare frigid: frigid is cold by nature, while frozen is cold by result.
normal.cn: 对比 frigid：frigid 是本性就冷，frozen 是被冻过之后才冷。

abstract.en: See a whole lake turn grey-white and hard as stone.
abstract.cn: 想象整片湖变成灰白色，硬得像石头。

abstract.en: Picture peas in a freezer drawer, still bright green under the ice.
abstract.cn: 想象冷冻柜抽屉里的豌豆，在冰下仍是鲜绿色。

abstract.en: Feel your fingers go white and lose all feeling in the snow.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在雪里变白，完全失去知觉。

examples.en: The lake was frozen to a depth of half a metre.
examples.cn: 湖面冻到半米深。

examples.en: Frozen vegetables keep most of their vitamins.
examples.cn: 冷冻蔬菜保留了大部分维生素。

examples.en: The company sold its frozen assets to pay the debt.
examples.cn: 公司卖掉冻结资产来还债。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗罗森」——末尾的 -en 像「已经……了」，正是 freeze 完成后留下的样子；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始印欧语重构词根 preus-（冻、冷）→ 原始日耳曼语 freusan（冻结）→ 古英语 freosan → 中古英语过去分词 frozen → 现代英语 frozen；核心义「被冻住、不再流动」。

sensesIntro.en: Frozen begins with water turned to ice, then covers food kept cold, numb flesh, blocked roads, fear that stops the body, money fixed in place, a face without warmth, and a machine that will not respond.
sensesIntro.cn: frozen 从水结成冰开始，继而指冷冻保存的食物、冻僵的血肉、封住的道路、把人定住的恐惧、被固定住的钱、没有暖意的脸，以及不肯响应的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole lake locked into a sheet of grey-white ice.
core.cn: 核心意象：整片湖被锁成一块灰白的冰。

branches.en: Water becoming ice and ice closing a route are the literal pair.
branches.cn: 水结成冰与冰封住道路是字面的一对。

branches.en: Food kept under ice gives the storage sense.
branches.cn: 冰下保存食物给出储藏义项。

branches.en: Numb flesh and a body stopped by fear share the stiffness of ice.
branches.cn: 冻僵的血肉与被恐惧定住的身体共享冰的僵硬。

branches.en: Money and rules frozen in place give the fixed sense.
branches.cn: 被冻在原地的钱与规则给出固定义项。

branches.en: A frozen face and a frozen screen both stop moving.
branches.cn: 僵住的脸与卡死的屏幕都停止运转。

definition_zh: 节俭的；简朴的；节约的；精打细算的
definition_en: careful with money and resources, simple and inexpensive, or sparing in the use of something
core_image: 补了又补的布袋，每一粒米都倒干净
scene: 月底只剩几枚硬币，她把每笔开销都记在本子上。A frugal household plans every purchase and wastes almost nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 frugal 是「节俭的」（第 1 个义项：花钱有节制、不浪费）；句意：节俭的家庭计划每一笔开销，几乎不浪费任何东西。

derivatives.zh: 节俭；节省
节俭地；节约地

senses.title: Careful with money
senses.definition: spending little and avoiding waste of money
senses.definitionCN: 花钱少、避免浪费钱财
senses.example: Her frugal parents saved enough to buy the shop outright.
senses.exampleCN: 她节俭的父母攒够了钱，把店铺整个买了下来。
senses.why: Latin frugalitas first named the worth of produce, and the adjective came to praise careful use rather than waste.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frugalitas 最初与农产的「价值」有关，这个形容词后来用来称赞精打细算而非浪费。

senses.title: Simple and inexpensive
senses.definition: plain and cheap, of a life, a meal, or a style
senses.definitionCN: 生活、饮食或风格朴素而花费少
senses.example: They had a frugal supper of bread and soup.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的晚餐很简朴，只有面包和汤。
senses.why: A plain meal costs little, so care with money shows on the table as simplicity.
senses.whyCN: 朴素的一餐花不了多少钱，于是用钱的谨慎在餐桌上表现为简单。

senses.title: Sparing in the use of resources
senses.definition: using fuel, water, or materials carefully so that little is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎使用燃料、水或材料，几乎不浪费
senses.example: The house is frugal with water in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这房子夏天很节约用水。
senses.why: The idea moves from coins to kilowatts: careful measuring keeps resources from being lost.
senses.whyCN: 这个观念从硬币走到千瓦：仔细计量能让资源不被白白流失。

senses.title: Meagre in amount
senses.definition: small and plain in quantity, of food, income, or a portion
senses.definitionCN: 食物、收入或份量少而简单
senses.example: The monks lived on a frugal allowance.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们靠一份微薄的供给生活。
senses.why: What is carefully measured can also be small, so thrift slides into meagreness.
senses.whyCN: 精打细算的东西也可能本来就少，于是节俭滑向「微薄」。

senses.title: Close to stinginess
senses.titleCN: 近乎吝啬的；过分节省的
senses.definition: excessively sparing, so that care turns into meanness
senses.definitionCN: 节省过度，以至于精打细算变成吝啬
senses.example: His frugal habits made him refuse to tip the waiter.
senses.exampleCN: 他过分节省的习惯让他连小费都不肯给侍者。
senses.why: Thrift praised becomes greed blamed when saving stops being reasonable.
senses.whyCN: 当节省越过合理的界限，被称赞的节俭就变成被指责的吝啬。

senses.title: Temperate in food and drink
senses.definition: moderate in eating and drinking, in an older use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：饮食有节制、不过量
senses.example: The physician advised a frugal diet and early hours.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议饮食有节制、早睡早起。
senses.why: Roman thrift covered the whole of life, so frugal once meant moderate at the table as well.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马的节俭观覆盖整个生活，所以 frugal 也曾指餐桌上的有度。

senses.title: Sparing with words
senses.definition: using few words, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 用词很少，往往是刻意的
senses.example: The editor was frugal with praise and with blame.
senses.exampleCN: 这位编辑无论是称赞还是责备都惜字如金。
senses.why: Words are a resource too, so the same care can be applied to speech.
senses.whyCN: 言辞也是一种资源，同样的精打细算可以用在说话上。

senses.title: Plain without ornament
senses.definition: plain and without decoration, of design or style
senses.definitionCN: 设计或风格朴素、不加装饰
senses.example: The chapel has a frugal beauty of bare stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小教堂有一种素净之美，只有裸露的石墙。
senses.why: A style that spends nothing on ornament looks frugal, so economy becomes an aesthetic.
senses.whyCN: 不在装饰上花钱的风格看起来就很 frugal，于是「省」成了一种美学。

intro.en: Frugal comes from Latin frugalis, thrifty, formed on frux, fruit or produce, and its worth.
intro.cn: frugal 来自拉丁语 frugalis（节俭的），由 frux（果实、出产）及其「价值」义构成。

items.en: Frux, frugis means fruit, produce, and by extension worth or value.
items.cn: frux、frugis 意为果实、出产，引申为价值。

items.en: Frui means to enjoy something or to make use of it.
items.cn: frui 意为享用某物或加以利用。

items.en: Frugalis describes what is useful and thrifty, formed from frux.
items.cn: frugalis 形容有用而节俭的，由 frux 构成。

items.en: Frugal enters French as a learned borrowing from Latin frugalis.
items.cn: frugal 作为书面借词从拉丁语 frugalis 进入法语。

items.en: English takes frugal from French and Latin as a word for thrift.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从法语与拉丁语借入 frugal，用作「节俭」之词。

items.en: Modern English extends frugal from money to meals, design, and speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把 frugal 从金钱扩展到餐食、设计与言辞。

note.en: Frugal is the adjective behind frugality, frugally, and frugalness, and it stands near thrifty, economical, and sparing.
note.cn: frugal 是 frugality、frugally、frugalness 背后的形容词，并与 thrifty、economical、sparing 相邻。

normal.en: Frugal starts with fru-, the same opening as fruit.
normal.cn: frugal 以 fru- 开头，和 fruit 的开头一样。

normal.en: Latin frux means fruit, and the adjective first praised good use of produce.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 frux 意为果实，这个形容词最初称赞的是对农产的好好利用。

normal.en: Frugal with money and frugal with water show the same care in two places.

normal.en: Frugality is the noun, frugally the adverb, and frugalness the quality.

normal.en: Compare thrifty: thrifty stresses saving, while frugal stresses plain and careful living.

abstract.en: See a cloth bag stitched again and again, with every grain of rice poured out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个补了又补的布袋，每一粒米都倒得干干净净。

abstract.en: Picture a supper of bread and soup on a bare wooden table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张光木桌上摆着面包与汤的晚餐。

abstract.en: Watch a water meter turn very slowly while the tap is open.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头开着，水表却转得极慢。

examples.en: A frugal cook wastes nothing and uses every part of the vegetable.
examples.cn: 节俭的厨子什么都不浪费，蔬菜的每一部分都用上。

examples.en: They chose a frugal holiday in the mountains instead of a resort.
examples.cn: 他们选择去山里过一个简朴的假期，而没去度假村。

examples.en: Frugal design keeps the building cheap to run.
examples.cn: 节俭的设计让这栋楼的运行成本很低。

branches.en: A small measured portion turns thrift into meagreness.
branches.cn: 量得仔细的一小份把节俭变成微薄。

branches.en: When saving goes too far, thrift is read as stinginess.

definition_zh: 节俭；节省；简朴；精打细算
definition_en: the habit or quality of being careful with money and resources and avoiding waste
core_image: 账本上一行行小字，每一项都比预算少一点
scene: 祖母把旧毛衣拆了重新织，线头都收进铁盒里。Her frugality was not a pose but a habit learned in years of scarcity.
sceneCN: 这里 frugality 是「节俭」（第 1 个义项：不浪费钱财的品质）；句意：她的节俭不是装出来的，而是匮乏年月里养成的习惯。

derivatives.zh: 节俭的；简朴的
节俭地；节约地
节俭；朴素（由 frugal 加 -ness 构成）

senses.title: Thrift as a settled habit
senses.definition: the habit of being careful with money and avoiding waste
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎用钱、避免浪费的习惯
senses.example: Frugality kept the family out of debt.
senses.exampleCN: 节俭让这个家庭没有背上债务。
senses.why: The Latin noun frugalitas named a settled virtue, so the first sense is the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 frugalitas 指一种稳定的德行，所以第一个义项就是这种习惯本身。

senses.title: Economy in spending
senses.definition: the practice of spending little and planning each purchase
senses.definitionCN: 少花钱并计划每一笔开支的做法
senses.example: Their frugality showed in the careful weekly budget.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的节约体现在仔细的每周预算里。
senses.why: Thrift becomes a practice when the habit is applied to the purse.
senses.whyCN: 当这种习惯落到钱包上，节俭就成了一种做法。

senses.title: A plain way of living
senses.definition: a simple life with few expensive things
senses.definitionCN: 少用昂贵物品的简单生活
senses.example: The monks were admired for the frugality of their daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们因日常生活的简朴而受敬重。
senses.why: Care with money shapes the whole household, so it turns into a plain way of living.
senses.whyCN: 对钱的谨慎会塑造整个家庭，于是它变成一种朴素的生活方式。

senses.title: Sparing use of resources
senses.definition: the careful use of materials, fuel, or water so that little is lost
senses.definitionCN: 对材料、燃料或水的谨慎使用，使浪费极少
senses.example: Frugality with water is a rule in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 节约用水在沙漠里是规矩。
senses.why: The habit can be applied to any resource, not only to coins.
senses.whyCN: 这种习惯可以用在任何资源上，不只用在钱币上。

senses.title: Low cost of a plan or design
senses.definition: the quality of costing little to build or to run
senses.definitionCN: 建造或运行花费少的性质
senses.example: The frugality of the design kept the house affordable.
senses.exampleCN: 设计的低成本让这栋房子价格可负担。
senses.why: A plan that asks little of the purse shows the same virtue as a person who saves.
senses.whyCN: 一个不向钱包多要钱的方案，与一个会攒钱的人显出同一种德行。

senses.title: Excess that looks like meanness
senses.definition: thrift carried so far that it becomes meanness
senses.definitionCN: 节俭走到极端而变成吝啬
senses.example: The frugality of the office showed in one tea bag shared by four staff.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的过分节省体现在四个人合用一个茶包。
senses.why: A virtue has a shadow: saving that refuses all pleasure is read as meanness.
senses.whyCN: 德行也有阴影：拒绝一切享受的节省会被读成吝啬。

senses.title: Moderation in food and drink
senses.definition: moderate eating and drinking, in an older use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：饮食有节制、不过量
senses.example: Doctors once praised the frugality of a simple diet.
senses.exampleCN: 医生曾称赞简单饮食带来的节制。
senses.why: Roman frugalitas covered the whole of life, including the table.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马的 frugalitas 覆盖整个生活，包括餐桌。

senses.title: Sparing use of time and energy
senses.definition: the careful use of time or energy so that none is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎使用时间或精力，一点也不浪费
senses.example: Her frugality with time meant no meeting ran past the hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她对时间的珍惜意味着没有一场会议超过一小时。
senses.why: Modern speakers extend the old virtue to time and effort, which are resources too.
senses.whyCN: 现代人把这古老的德行延伸到时间与精力，它们同样是资源。

scene: 果园里，整排果树都挂着沉甸甸的果子。Every tree in the orchard looked fruitful that autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 fruitful 是「果实累累的」（第 1 个义项：结出很多果实）；句意：那年秋天，果园里每棵树都果实累累。

pos.zh: 多产的；果实累累的；富有成效的；肥沃的

derivatives.zh: 由 fruitful 加 -ly 构成，义为「富有成效地」
由 fruitful 加 -ness 构成，义为「多产；成效」
由 un- 加 fruitful 构成，义为「不结果的；无成效的」
由 fruit 加 -less 构成，义为「无结果的；徒劳的」

senses.title: Bearing much fruit
senses.definition: producing a large amount of fruit
senses.definitionCN: 结出大量果实
senses.example: The old apple tree is still fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老苹果树仍然果实累累。
senses.why: Fruit plus the suffix -ful, meaning full of, gives the literal picture of a tree loaded with fruit.
senses.whyCN: fruit 加上表示「充满」的后缀 -ful，字面画面就是一棵挂满果实的树。

senses.title: Producing good results
senses.definition: yielding useful results or benefits
senses.definitionCN: 产生有用的结果或好处
senses.example: Their long talks proved fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 他们长时间的商谈证明是富有成效的。
senses.why: When a plan bears fruit, the harvest image moves from the orchard to any effort that ends in a result.
senses.whyCN: 当计划「结果」时，收割的意象就从果园移到了任何以成果收尾的努力上。

senses.title: Fertile and able to bear crops
senses.definition: of land or soil, able to produce healthy crops
senses.definitionCN: 指土地或土壤能长出好庄稼
senses.example: The valley soil is dark and fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里的土壤又黑又肥沃。
senses.why: Land that carries fruit well is land that is fertile, so the fruit image comes to name the ground itself.
senses.whyCN: 能好好承载果实的土地就是肥沃的土地，于是果实意象转而命名土地本身。

senses.title: Rich in something
senses.definition: producing or supplying something in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 大量产生或提供某物
senses.example: The archive is a fruitful source of local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这座档案馆是地方史料的丰富来源。
senses.why: The idea of a full harvest widens into any place or source that keeps giving.
senses.whyCN: 丰收的观念扩展为任何不断给出东西的场所或来源。

senses.title: Able to have children
senses.definition: literary or biblical: able to produce many children
senses.definitionCN: 书面或圣经用法：能生育许多子女
senses.example: The old blessing told the family to be fruitful.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的祝福要这个家族多多生养。
senses.why: The oldest sense of fruit is offspring, so fruitful describes a person or family that multiplies.
senses.whyCN: fruit 最古老的义项是子嗣，所以 fruitful 描述的是不断添丁的人或家族。

senses.title: Busy and productive
senses.definition: of a period or career, full of activity and achievement
senses.definitionCN: 指一段时间或职业生涯活动多且有成就
senses.example: It was a fruitful decade for the small firm.
senses.exampleCN: 对这间小公司来说，那是收获丰硕的十年。
senses.why: A span of time is pictured as a tree: what it yields is measured in results rather than apples.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间被比作一棵树：它结出的不是苹果，而是用成果来衡量的东西。

intro.en: Fruitful joins fruit, from Latin fructus, with the suffix -ful, and has meant full of fruit since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: fruitful 由 fruit（源自拉丁语 fructus）加后缀 -ful 构成，中世纪起就表示「结满果实」。

items.en: Frui means to enjoy or to use, and fructus means fruit, produce, or profit.
items.cn: frui 意为享用、使用，fructus 意为果实、收成或收益。

items.en: Frux, frugis names fruit or crops in older Latin.
items.cn: 较早的拉丁语用 frux、frugis 指果实或庄稼。

items.en: Fruit passes into Old French with the meaning fruit or profit.
items.cn: fruit 进入古法语，意为果实或收益。

items.en: English fruit names the produce of a tree or the profit of an effort.
items.cn: 英语 fruit 指树的产物，也指努力的收益。

items.en: The adjective fruitful forms with -ful, full of fruit.
items.cn: 形容词 fruitful 由 -ful 构成，意为「满是果实」。

items.en: Modern English extends fruitful to discussions, research, and careers.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fruitful 扩展到讨论、研究与职业生涯。

note.en: Fruitful belongs to the fruit family, and its near meanings cluster around producing results.
note.cn: fruitful 属于 fruit 词族，近义词则围绕「产生结果」聚在一起。

entries.definition: the seed-bearing product of a plant
producing no result
in a productive way
producing much or achieving a lot
able to produce crops or young
producing a great deal

normalIntro.en: Fruitful is built from the plain word fruit plus the suffix -ful, so the memory is a tree so loaded that its branches bend.
normalIntro.cn: fruitful 由普通的 fruit 加后缀 -ful 构成，记忆画面是一棵果实太重、把枝条压弯的树。

normal.en: Fruit plus -ful means full of fruit, the literal orchard picture.
normal.cn: fruit 加 -ful 就是「满是果实」，这是果园里的字面画面。

normal.en: A fruitful meeting bears fruit: it ends with decisions, not just talk.
normal.cn: 富有成效的会议会「结果」：结束时带来决定，而不只是谈话。

normal.en: Fruitless is its opposite: no fruit, no result.
normal.cn: fruitless 是它的反面：没有果实，没有结果。

normal.en: We say a plan bears fruit, and a fruitful plan is one that worked.
normal.cn: 我们说计划「结果」，而富有成效的计划就是奏效的计划。

normal.en: Soil that is fruitful is simply soil that can carry a crop.
normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤不过是能承载庄稼的土壤。

abstract.en: See a branch bending under red apples until it almost touches the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一根枝条被红苹果压弯，几乎垂到草地上。

abstract.en: See a sheet of paper with a long list of ticked boxes after a meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象会议结束后，纸上有一长串打了勾的条目。

abstract.en: See dark soil holding rows of green shoots.
abstract.cn: 想象深色土壤里立着一排排绿芽。

examples.en: The garden stayed fruitful even in a dry summer.
examples.cn: 即使夏天干旱，园子仍然果实累累。

examples.en: Years of patient talks finally proved fruitful.
examples.cn: 多年的耐心商谈终于有了成效。

examples.en: They met to look for a fruitful way to share the land.
examples.cn: 他们会面，想找到一种富有成效的方式共享这片土地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fruitful」读起来近「福禄透」——福气与收成多到透出来，正是「结满果实」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 frui（享用、使用）→ fructus（果实、收成）→ 古法语 fruit → 英语 fruit；加后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成 fruitful，核心义「结满果实」。

sensesIntro.en: Fruitful starts with trees and land that carry fruit, then moves to any effort that yields good results, and finally to fertile people and busy periods.
sensesIntro.cn: fruitful 从结果子的树与土地出发，转向带来好结果的努力，最后指能生育的人与有收获的时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch so heavy with fruit that it bends.
core.cn: 核心意象：果实压弯的枝条。

branches.en: The orchard sense is the literal heart of the word.
branches.cn: 果园义是这个字最字面的核心。

branches.en: Results in work and in a stretch of time both grow from the harvest image.
branches.cn: 工作成果与一段时间的收获都来自收割意象。

branches.en: Fertile ground keeps the image close to soil.
branches.cn: 肥沃土地让意象贴近土壤。

branches.en: Any generous source is pictured as a tree that keeps giving.
branches.cn: 任何丰沛的来源都被比作不断结果的树。

branches.en: Offspring is the oldest fruit, so family growth belongs here too.
branches.cn: 子嗣是最古老的「果实」，家族繁衍也归入此列。

intro.en: Fruitful is a transparent English build: the noun fruit plus the adjective suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fruitful 是透明的英语构词：名词 fruit 加形容词后缀 -ful。

latinIntro.en: Latin frui, to enjoy, and fructus, fruit or produce, supply the base of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frui（享用）与 fructus（果实、收成）提供这个词族的基础。

items.example: Frui is the old verb behind the fruit family.
items.exampleCN: frui 是 fruit 词族背后的古老动词。

items.example: Fructus gives both the crop and the profit.
items.exampleCN: fructus 同时给出庄稼与收益。

items.example: Frux is the older noun for what the field yields.
items.exampleCN: frux 是更古老的词，指田地所出。

items.example: Old French fruit carries both senses.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 fruit 兼有两种含义。

items.example: English fruit keeps the concrete sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语 fruit 保留具体含义。

items.example: The suffix -ful turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Fruitful joins the noun and the suffix.
items.exampleCN: fruitful 把名词与后缀结合在一起。

items.example: The adverb adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 副词在形容词后加 -ly。

items.example: The noun adds -ness.
items.exampleCN: 名词形式加 -ness。

items.example: The negative partner adds -less.
items.exampleCN: 反义形式加 -less。

definition_zh: 挫败；阻挠；使落空；使沮丧
definition_en: to prevent a plan or effort from succeeding, or to make someone feel annoyed and discouraged
core_image: 门被推开的一刻，又被从里面顶了回去
scene: 项目组连夜赶出的方案，在评审会上被一句话否决。The sudden veto frustrated months of careful planning.
sceneCN: 这里 frustrate 是「使受挫、使无法实现」（第 1 个义项：阻挠计划或努力）；句意：突然的否决让数月精心筹划付诸东流。

pos.zh: 挫败；阻挠；使落空；使沮丧

derivatives.zh: 由 frustrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「阻挠；沮丧」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「令人沮丧的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「受挫的；沮丧的」
由 frustrating 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人沮丧地」

senses.title: To block a plan or attempt
senses.definition: to prevent a plan, attempt, or effort from succeeding
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、尝试或努力无法成功
senses.example: Bad weather frustrated the rescue attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣天气使救援行动受挫。
senses.why: Latin frustra means in vain, so the verb first means to make an effort come to nothing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frustra 意为徒然，所以这个动词最早指让努力化为乌有。

senses.title: To make someone feel annoyed and discouraged
senses.definition: to make a person feel annoyed and powerless because a goal is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 因目标受阻而让人感到恼火、无力
senses.example: Slow replies frustrated the customers.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的回复让顾客很恼火。
senses.why: When a person is blocked again and again, the outward blocking turns into an inner feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人一再被挡住，外在的阻碍就转成了内心的感受。

senses.title: To make an effort useless
senses.definition: to cause effort, hope, or expectation to bring no result
senses.definitionCN: 使努力、希望或期待毫无结果
senses.example: The new rules frustrated every hope of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让一切改革的希望落空。
senses.why: The core idea of making something vain applies to hope itself, not only to action.
senses.whyCN: 「使某事徒然」的核心不只用于行动，也用于希望本身。

senses.title: To defeat or invalidate in law
senses.definition: legal or technical: to defeat a claim, purpose, or legal effect
senses.definitionCN: 法律或技术用法：使主张、目的或法律效力失效
senses.example: The court frustrated the purpose of the clause.
senses.exampleCN: 法院使该条款的目的落空。
senses.why: Legal language borrows the verb for any rule or claim that is blocked from taking effect.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言借这个动词表示任何被挡住、无法生效的规则或主张。

senses.title: To block a need in psychology
senses.definition: psychology: to block a drive or need so that inner tension builds up
senses.definitionCN: 心理学：阻挡某种驱力或需求，使内心紧张积累
senses.example: Repeated delays frustrated the children until they stopped trying.
senses.exampleCN: 一再的拖延让孩子们受挫，最后他们不再尝试。
senses.why: Psychology names the inner state that appears when a drive is repeatedly blocked.
senses.whyCN: 心理学命名的是驱力被反复阻挡时出现的内心状态。

intro.en: Frustrate comes from Latin frustrari, to deceive or disappoint, which rests on the adverb frustra, in vain.
intro.cn: frustrate 来自拉丁语 frustrari（欺骗、使失望），其基础是副词 frustra（徒然、白费）。

items.en: Frustra is an adverb meaning in vain or without effect.
items.cn: frustra 是副词，意为徒然、没有效果。

items.en: Frustrari means to deceive, to disappoint, or to bring to nothing.
items.cn: frustrari 意为欺骗、使失望或使化为乌有。

items.en: Frustratio names a deception or a disappointment; a link to fraus, fraud, is often suggested but not certain.
items.cn: frustratio 指欺骗或失望；它与 fraus（欺诈）的联系常被提起，但并不可靠。

items.en: Old French frustrer takes the verb in the sense to render vain.
items.cn: 古法语 frustrer 取「使徒劳」之义。

items.en: Middle English frustraten records the verb in learned use.
items.cn: 中古英语 frustraten 在学术语用中记录了这个动词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the outward sense of blocking and adds the inner sense of annoyance.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「阻挡」的外在义，又加入「恼火」的内心义。

note.en: Frustrate is the verb of making efforts vain; its family includes frustration, frustrating, and frustrated, and its near meanings are about blocking.
note.cn: frustrate 是「让努力落空」的动词，词族包括 frustration、frustrating、frustrated，近义词都与「阻挡」有关。

entries.definition: the state of being blocked or annoyed
causing annoyance by blocking progress
annoyed because a goal is blocked
to stop a plan from being carried out
to prevent an attempt from succeeding
to make progress slow or difficult

normalIntro.en: Frustrate is built on Latin frustra, in vain: the word names what happens when effort is made to come to nothing.
normalIntro.cn: frustrate 建立在拉丁语 frustra（徒然）之上：它命名的正是努力化为乌有时发生的事。

normal.en: Frustra means in vain, and frustrate is to make something come to nothing.
normal.cn: frustra 意为徒然，frustrate 就是使某事化为乌有。

normal.en: Frustrate a plan and the plan stops; frustrate a person and the person feels stopped.
normal.cn: 挫败计划，计划就停下；挫败一个人，这个人就感到被卡住。

normal.en: Frustrate and frustration differ only by the noun ending -ion.
normal.cn: frustrate 与 frustration 只差名词词尾 -ion。

normal.en: Frustrating describes the thing that blocks you; frustrated describes you.
normal.cn: frustrating 描述挡住你的东西，frustrated 描述你自己。

normal.en: Compare thwart: thwart is more neutral, while frustrate adds the feeling of wasted effort.
normal.cn: 对比 thwart：thwart 更中性，frustrate 多了「努力白费」的意味。

abstract.en: See a door slamming shut just as you push it open.
abstract.cn: 想象你刚把门推开，门又砰地关上。

abstract.en: See a person pressing a lift button that never lights up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人反复按电梯按钮，灯却始终不亮。

abstract.en: See a bubble of hope touched by a finger and gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个希望的泡泡被手指一碰就破了。

examples.en: Heavy rain frustrated the rescue attempt.
examples.cn: 大雨使救援行动受挫。

examples.en: The endless delays frustrated everyone in the queue.
examples.cn: 无休止的拖延让队伍里每个人都很恼火。

examples.en: A good teacher does not frustrate a child who learns slowly.
examples.cn: 好老师不会让学得慢的孩子感到挫败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「frus-」读起来像「烦死」：事情被挡住，人自然烦死——这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 frustra（徒然、白费）→ frustrari（欺骗、使落空）→ 古法语 frustrer → 英语 frustrate，核心义「让努力落空」。

sensesIntro.en: Frustrate begins with the outward act of blocking a plan, then names the inner annoyance of a blocked person, then the wasting of hope, a legal use, and finally the psychological blocking of a need.
sensesIntro.cn: frustrate 先指从外面阻挠计划，再指被挡住的人内心的恼火，继而指希望落空、法律上的失效，最后指心理学意义上的需求受阻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door pushed open, then slammed back at the last moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：门被推开的一刻，又被从里面顶回去。

branches.en: The outward act of blocking a plan is the root sense.
branches.cn: 从外面阻挠计划是这个词的根义。

branches.en: Annoyance and psychological tension are the same blocking moved inward.
branches.cn: 恼火与心理紧张是同一个阻挡转向内心的结果。

branches.en: Hope made vain extends the block from action to expectation.
branches.cn: 希望落空把阻挡从行动扩展到期待。

branches.en: Law borrows the verb for a claim that cannot take effect.
branches.cn: 法律借用这个动词表示无法生效的主张。

branches.en: Both a stopped attempt and a wasted hope end in the same nothing.
branches.cn: 被拦下的尝试与白费的希望，最终都归于同样的「无」。

intro.en: Frustrate is a learned Latin verb in English, with the noun frustration and the two participles built around it.
intro.cn: frustrate 是英语中的学术性拉丁动词，围绕它构成名词 frustration 与两个分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin frustra, in vain, and frustrari, to disappoint, supply the base of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frustra（徒然）与 frustrari（使失望）提供这个词族的基础。

items.example: Frustra states the result the verb aims at.
items.exampleCN: frustra 道出这个动词所指向的结果。

items.example: Frustrari is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: frustrari 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Frustratio gives the abstract noun its shape.
items.exampleCN: frustratio 给了抽象名词以形态。

items.example: Old French frustrer carries the verb onward.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 frustrer 把动词继续带下去。

items.example: English frustrate keeps the active sense.
items.exampleCN: 英语 frustrate 保留主动含义。

items.example: The ending -ate marks a learned verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 标示学术性动词。

items.meaning: the act or state of being blocked
items.example: The noun adds -ion to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词在动词后加 -ion。

items.example: The participle adds -ing.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式加 -ing。

items.example: The participle adds -ed.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式加 -ed。

items.example: The adverb adds -ly.
items.exampleCN: 副词形式加 -ly。

definition_zh: 令人沮丧的；使人恼火的；难有成效的
definition_en: causing someone to feel annoyed or discouraged because progress is blocked
core_image: 钥匙在锁孔里转不动，门始终不开
scene: 队伍排了很久，前面的人却始终不动。The long wait in the queue was deeply frustrating.
sceneCN: 这里 frustrating 是「令人沮丧的」（第 1 个义项：因进展受阻而让人恼火）；句意：在队伍里久等，让人十分沮丧。

pos.zh: 令人沮丧的；使人恼火的；难有成效的

collocations.zh: 越来越令人沮丧的过程

derivatives.zh: 由 frustrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「沮丧；阻挠」
基础动词，义为「挫败；使落空」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「受挫的；沮丧的」
由 frustrating 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人沮丧地」

senses.title: Causing annoyance by blocking progress
senses.titleCN: 令人恼火的；使人受挫的
senses.definition: making someone feel annoyed because what they want to do is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 因为想做的事被挡住而让人恼火
senses.example: It was frustrating to watch the slow queue.
senses.exampleCN: 看着缓慢挪动的队伍，真让人恼火。
senses.why: The present participle of frustrate turns the act of blocking into a quality that a situation has.
senses.whyCN: frustrate 的现在分词把「阻挡」这个动作变成了情境自身具备的性质。

senses.title: Hard to deal with and giving little reward
senses.definition: difficult and tiring, with little chance of a good result
senses.definitionCN: 困难又累人，得到好结果的机会很小
senses.example: Cleaning the old files was frustrating work.
senses.exampleCN: 清理旧档案是件费力又难见成效的工作。
senses.why: An effort that keeps meeting resistance is pictured as a thing that frustrates everyone who touches it.
senses.whyCN: 一再遇到阻力的努力，被比作一件让每个接触它的人都受挫的东西。

senses.title: Causing disappointment by falling short
senses.definition: making people disappointed because the result is worse than expected
senses.definitionCN: 因结果不如预期而让人失望
senses.example: The team suffered a frustrating draw.
senses.exampleCN: 球队遭遇了一场令人失望的平局。
senses.why: A result that stops short of the goal blocks expectation, and the participle names that disappointment.
senses.whyCN: 结果差一点没达到目标，就挡住了期待，分词形式正是命名这种失望。

senses.title: Repeatedly blocking what one wants
senses.definition: of a situation, repeatedly preventing someone from doing what they intend
senses.definitionCN: 指情境一再阻止人做想做的事
senses.example: The broken printer made the morning frustrating for all of us.
senses.exampleCN: 坏掉的打印机让我们的早晨一再受挫。
senses.why: The -ing form suggests an ongoing action, so the adjective suits a block that repeats.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式带有「持续进行」的意味，所以这个形容词适合反复出现的阻挡。

senses.title: Producing a feeling of tension
senses.definition: causing inner tension that builds up over time
senses.definitionCN: 使内心的紧张随着时间不断积累
senses.example: Months of frustrating talks ended without a deal.
senses.exampleCN: 数月令人焦躁的商谈最终没有达成协议。
senses.why: When a block lasts, annoyance hardens into tension, and the adjective can name that slow build-up.
senses.whyCN: 当阻挡持续下去，恼火会硬化成紧张，这个形容词也能命名这种缓慢的积累。

intro.en: Frustrating is the present participle of frustrate, from Latin frustrari, and it became an adjective in its own right.
intro.cn: frustrating 是 frustrate 的现在分词，源自拉丁语 frustrari，后来独立成形容词。

items.en: Frustra is an adverb meaning in vain.

items.en: Frustrari means to deceive or to disappoint.

items.en: Old French frustrer carries the verb with the sense to render vain.
items.cn: 古法语 frustrer 带着「使徒劳」的含义承接这个动词。

items.en: The participle frustrating is recorded as an adjective describing situations.
items.cn: 分词 frustrating 被记录为描述情境的形容词。

items.en: Modern English uses frustrating for tasks, delays, and people alike.
items.cn: 现代英语把 frustrating 用于任务、延误和人。

note.en: Frustrating is the -ing adjective of the verb frustrate, and its near meanings describe things that wear patience down.
note.cn: frustrating 是动词 frustrate 的 -ing 形容词，近义词都描述消磨耐心的东西。

normalIntro.en: Frustrating is the -ing adjective of frustrate: it describes what the situation does to you, not what you feel.
normalIntro.cn: frustrating 是 frustrate 的 -ing 形容词：它描述情境对你做了什么，而不是你感受到了什么。

normal.en: The ending -ing marks the thing that causes the feeling; -ed marks the person who feels it.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ing 标示引起感受的事物，-ed 标示产生感受的人。

normal.en: A frustrating delay blocks you; a frustrated traveller waits.
normal.cn: 令人恼火的延误挡住你，受挫的旅客在等待。

normal.en: The noun frustration names the feeling; the adjective frustrating names the cause.
normal.cn: 名词 frustration 命名感受，形容词 frustrating 命名原因。

normal.en: Compare annoying: frustrating adds the idea of wasted effort.
normal.cn: 对比 annoying：frustrating 多了「努力白费」的意味。

normal.en: Latin frustra, in vain, is still visible behind the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 frustra（徒然）仍能在这个词背后看见。

abstract.en: See a key turning in a lock that will not open.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里转动，锁却怎么也打不开。

abstract.en: See a person sweeping a floor while someone keeps dropping paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人扫地，另一个人却不断往地上扔纸。

abstract.en: See a scoreboard stuck one goal short of the target.
abstract.cn: 想象记分牌停在离目标只差一分的位置。

examples.en: Waiting for a reply all week was frustrating.
examples.cn: 整整一周等不到回复，让人十分沮丧。

examples.en: It is frustrating when the computer loses your work.
examples.cn: 电脑把做好的东西弄丢时，真让人恼火。

examples.en: The most frustrating part was not knowing the reason.
examples.cn: 最令人沮丧的是不知道原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「frus-」听起来像「烦死」，「-ing」表示正在——正在让人烦死的，就是「令人沮丧的」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

sensesIntro.en: Frustrating moves from the plain annoyance of a blocked goal to tiring work, a disappointing result, a block that repeats, and finally a tension that builds up.
sensesIntro.cn: frustrating 从目标受阻带来的恼火，转到费力的工作、令人失望的结果、反复出现的阻挡，最后指慢慢积累的紧张。

branches.cn: 目标被挡带来的单纯恼火是中心义项。

branches.en: Effort that meets constant resistance becomes tiring work.
branches.cn: 不断遇到阻力的努力就变成累人的工作。

branches.en: A result just short of the goal produces disappointment.
branches.cn: 差一点没达到目标的结果产生失望。

branches.en: The -ing ending lets the adjective describe a block that repeats.
branches.cn: -ing 词尾让这个形容词能描述反复出现的阻挡。

branches.en: Lasting annoyance slowly hardens into tension.
branches.cn: 持久的恼火慢慢硬化成紧张。

definition_zh: 沮丧；挫折感；阻挠；使人受挫的事
definition_en: the annoyed and discouraged feeling that comes when a goal is blocked, or the act of blocking it
core_image: 拳头握紧，掌心却什么也没有
scene: 他反复试着打开那扇卡住的门，最后把工具丢在地上。After ten tries he threw the tool down in frustration.
sceneCN: 这里 frustration 是「沮丧、挫折感」（第 1 个义项：目标受阻而生出的恼火与无力）；句意：试了十次之后，他把工具一摔，满心沮丧。

pos.zh: 沮丧；挫折感；阻挠；使人受挫的事

senses.title: The feeling of being blocked
senses.definition: the annoyed and powerless feeling that comes when a goal is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 目标受阻时产生的恼火与无力感
senses.example: She slammed the drawer in frustration.
senses.exampleCN: 她沮丧地把抽屉摔上。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of blocking into the feeling that stays with the person afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式把「阻挡」这个动作，变成事后留在人身上的感受。

senses.title: The act of blocking a plan
senses.definition: the act of preventing a plan or effort from succeeding
senses.definitionCN: 阻止计划或努力成功的行为
senses.example: The frustration of the reform was a loss for the city.
senses.exampleCN: 改革受挫是这座城市的一大损失。
senses.why: Latin frustratio named a deception, so the noun can still point to the blocking itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frustratio 本指欺骗，所以这个名词仍可指向「阻挡」这一行为本身。

senses.title: Something that blocks or disappoints
senses.definition: an event or condition that blocks what someone wants
senses.definitionCN: 挡住某人愿望的事件或状况
senses.example: Everyday frustrations wear people down.
senses.exampleCN: 日常的种种挫折消磨着人。
senses.why: A countable frustration is the concrete obstacle that produces the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 可数的 frustration 就是产生这种感受的具体障碍。

senses.title: A blocked need in psychology
senses.definition: psychology: the state produced when a drive or need cannot be satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 心理学：驱力或需求无法满足时产生的状态
senses.example: The study measured frustration in rats that could not reach food.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量了够不到食物的老鼠的受挫状态。
senses.why: Psychology gives the everyday feeling a technical name for a blocked drive.
senses.whyCN: 心理学给这种日常感受一个技术名称，专指驱力受阻。

senses.title: Long-term public dissatisfaction
senses.definition: a dissatisfaction with a situation that grows over time and is shared by many
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间积累、为许多人所共有的一种不满
senses.example: Public frustration with the delays grew through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 公众对延误的不满整个冬天都在增长。
senses.why: When a block lasts for a whole group, the private feeling becomes a public mood.
senses.whyCN: 当阻挡持续影响一整群人，私人的感受就变成了公共情绪。

intro.en: Frustration comes from Latin frustratio, a deception or disappointment, built on frustra, in vain.
intro.cn: frustration 来自拉丁语 frustratio（欺骗、失望），其基础是 frustra（徒然）。

items.en: Frustra is an adverb meaning in vain or without effect.
items.cn: frustra 是副词，意为徒然、没有效果。

items.en: Frustrari means to deceive, disappoint, or bring to nothing.
items.cn: frustrari 意为欺骗、使失望或使化为乌有。

items.en: Frustratio names a deception or a disappointment.
items.cn: frustratio 指欺骗或失望。

items.en: Old French frustrer carries the verb onward.
items.cn: 古法语 frustrer 把动词承接下去。

items.en: The noun frustration appears in English for a thwarted purpose.
items.cn: 名词 frustration 在英语中出现，指目的受挫。

items.en: Modern English adds the psychological sense of a blocked need.
items.cn: 现代英语加入「需求受阻」的心理学含义。

normal.en: The ending -ion turns the verb frustrate into the state that follows a block.

normal.en: Frustration is what you feel; frustrating is what caused it.
normal.cn: frustration 是你感受到的，frustrating 是造成它的东西。

normal.en: In frustration means with that feeling showing in a gesture or a voice.
normal.cn: in frustration 表示那种感受通过动作或语气表现出来。

normal.en: Latin frustra, in vain, explains why the word tastes of wasted effort.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 frustra（徒然）解释了为什么这个词带着「努力白费」的味道。

normal.en: Compare disappointment: disappointment looks back at a result, frustration at a block.

abstract.en: See a fist that tightens and then opens with nothing inside.

abstract.en: See a road sign turned to face the wrong direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌被转向了错误的方向。

abstract.en: See a small stone in a shoe that stops a long walk.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里的一颗小石子让长途行走停了下来。

examples.en: She walked out of the room in frustration.
examples.cn: 她沮丧地走出了房间。

examples.en: Years of frustration ended when the dam was finally approved.
examples.cn: 水坝最终获批，多年的挫败感随之结束。

examples.en: The job brings daily frustrations but also small rewards.
examples.cn: 这份工作带来日常的种种挫折，也带来小小的回报。

sensesIntro.en: Frustration starts as the feeling left by a block, then names the blocking itself, the obstacle that causes it, a blocked drive in psychology, and finally a shared public mood.
sensesIntro.cn: frustration 先指阻挡留下的感受，再指阻挡行为本身、造成它的障碍、心理学上的驱力受阻，最后指群体共有的公共情绪。

branches.en: The noun can still name the act of blocking itself.

branches.en: An obstacle and a blocked drive are both concrete sources of the state.
branches.cn: 具体障碍与受阻驱力都是这种状态的具体来源。

branches.en: A block shared by many turns a feeling into a public mood.
branches.cn: 众人共有的阻挡把感受变成公共情绪。

branches.en: The act and the feeling differ only in which side of the block you stand on.
branches.cn: 行为与感受的区别只在于你站在阻挡的哪一侧。

definition_zh: 逃亡者；逃犯；逃亡的；短暂的
definition_en: a person who flees or escapes, or something that lasts only a short time
core_image: 一个身影翻过低墙，头也不回地跑进夜色
scene: 警笛响起时，那个人翻过后墙消失在小巷里。The fugitive was last seen running toward the river.
sceneCN: 这里 fugitive 是「逃亡者」（第 1 个义项：为逃避追捕而逃跑的人）；句意：那名逃亡者最后一次被人看见，是朝河边跑去。

derivatives.zh: 由 fugitive 加 -ly 构成，义为「短暂地；逃亡地」
由 fugitive 加 -ness 构成，义为「短暂性；易逝」

senses.title: A person who flees
senses.definition: a person who escapes or runs away, especially from the law or from danger
senses.definitionCN: 为逃避法律或危险而逃跑的人
senses.example: The fugitive crossed the border at night.
senses.exampleCN: 那名逃亡者在夜里越过了边境。
senses.why: Latin fugitivus describes anyone apt to flee, and the noun use keeps that person in flight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fugitivus 描述任何易于逃跑的人，名词用法把这个人保持在「逃亡中」的状态。

senses.title: Fleeing or having escaped
senses.definition: adjective: fleeing, or having escaped from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 形容词：正在逃跑，或已从某地、某人手中逃脱
senses.example: The fugitive driver was stopped at the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 那名在逃的司机在桥上被拦下。
senses.why: The same Latin adjective modifies a person, so the word works as a description as well as a name.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁形容词也能修饰人，所以这个词既可作称呼，也可作描述。

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: lasting a very short time and hard to keep
senses.definitionCN: 只持续很短时间、难以留住
senses.example: He caught a fugitive glimpse of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 他瞥见月亮一眼，转瞬即逝。
senses.why: What flees does not stay, so the flight image stretches from people to moments and impressions.
senses.whyCN: 会逃走的东西不会停留，于是「逃跑」的意象从人延伸到时刻与印象。

senses.title: Wandering, roving
senses.definition: literary: moving from place to place without staying
senses.definitionCN: 书面用法：不停迁移、不作停留
senses.example: They led a fugitive life along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着海岸过着飘泊的生活。
senses.why: A person who keeps moving is always leaving, which is the original flight sense in a softer form.
senses.whyCN: 不断迁移的人总在离开，这正是「逃跑」本义较柔和的形态。

senses.title: Fading quickly in use
senses.definition: technical: of a colour or substance, fading or changing quickly
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：指颜色或物质很快褪去或变化
senses.example: The fugitive dye faded within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这种易褪的染料一年内就褪色了。
senses.why: Colours that will not stay are described with the same word for things that run away.
senses.whyCN: 留不住的颜色，也用这个表示「跑掉」的词来描述。

senses.title: Brief occasional writing
senses.definition: literary: of a poem or piece, written for an occasion and not meant to last
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法：为某个场合写就、不打算长存的作品
senses.example: The library keeps a box of fugitive poems.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆存着一箱即兴短诗。
senses.why: Occasional verse was expected to vanish with the day it marked, so it borrowed the flight word.
senses.whyCN: 应景诗本就被期待随所纪念的那一天一同消失，于是借用了「飞逝」这个词。

intro.en: Fugitive comes from Latin fugitivus, fleeing, from fugere, to flee, and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: fugitive 来自拉丁语 fugitivus（逃跑的），源于 fugere（逃跑），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root bheug means to flee.
items.cn: 重构词根 bheug 意为逃跑。

items.en: Fugere means to flee, and fuga means a flight.
items.cn: fugere 意为逃跑，fuga 意为逃亡。

items.en: Fugitivus, built on fugere, means fleeing or apt to flee.
items.cn: 由 fugere 构成的 fugitivus 意为逃跑的、易逃的。

items.en: Old French fugitif carries the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 fugitif 兼有形容词与名词用法。

items.en: Middle English fugitif names a person who has escaped.
items.cn: 中古英语 fugitif 指已经逃脱的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of something fleeting and hard to keep.
items.cn: 现代英语加入「短暂、难以留住」的含义。

note.en: Fugitive belongs to the Latin flight family, and its near meanings divide between people who run and things that do not last.
note.cn: fugitive 属于拉丁语「逃跑」词族，近义词分成「逃跑的人」与「不长久的事物」两类。

normalIntro.en: Fugitive comes from Latin fugere, to flee: the whole word rests on the picture of running away.
normalIntro.cn: fugitive 来自拉丁语 fugere（逃跑）：整个词都建立在「跑开」的画面上。

normal.en: Fugere means to flee, and fugitivus means ready to flee.
normal.cn: fugere 意为逃跑，fugitivus 意为随时要逃的。

normal.en: A fugitive is a person in flight; a fugitive glimpse is a moment in flight.
normal.cn: fugitive 可以是逃跑中的人，也可以是飞逝的一瞥。

normal.en: Compare refuge: a refuge is the place you flee to, a fugitive is the one who flees.
normal.cn: 对比 refuge：避难所是你逃向的地方，逃亡者是逃跑的那个人。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes an adjective, as in fugitive moments that will not stay.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 构成形容词，如 fugitive moments 指留不住的片刻。

normal.en: Fugue, the musical form, comes from the same flight image of one voice chasing another.
normal.cn: 赋格曲 fugue 也来自同样的追逐意象：一个声部追着另一个声部。

abstract.en: See a figure climbing a low wall and dropping into the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人影翻过低墙，落进黑暗里。

abstract.en: See a torch beam sweeping an empty road.
abstract.cn: 想象一束手电光扫过空荡荡的公路。

abstract.en: See a soap bubble that lasts for one breath.
abstract.cn: 想象一个肥皂泡只存在一次呼吸的时间。

examples.en: The fugitive hid in a barn until the search ended.
examples.cn: 那名逃亡者躲在谷仓里，直到搜索结束。

examples.en: Police warned that the fugitive might still be armed.
examples.cn: 警方警告说，那名逃犯可能仍带着武器。

examples.en: Fame can be fugitive, gone as quickly as it came.
examples.cn: 名声可能转瞬即逝，来得快去得也快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fug-」读起来像「飞个」——飞快逃走的一个人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fugere（逃跑）→ fuga（逃亡）→ fugitivus（逃跑的）→ 古法语 fugitif → 英语 fugitive，核心义「逃离而去」。

sensesIntro.en: Fugitive begins with the person who runs, then the adjective for someone in flight, then anything that passes quickly, a wandering life, unstable colour, and finally verse written for a day.
sensesIntro.cn: fugitive 先指逃跑的人，再作形容词指在逃的，继而指一切飞快消逝之物、飘泊的生活、不稳定的颜色，最后指为某一天写就的诗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure going over a wall into the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：翻墙没入夜色的人影。

branches.en: The person who flees is the literal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 逃跑的人是这个词最字面的中心。

branches.en: The adjective keeps the same person, only described rather than named.
branches.cn: 形容词用法保留同一个人，只是描述而非称呼。

branches.en: Moments and colours both fly away, so both take the flight word.
branches.cn: 时刻与颜色都会飞逝，所以都借用了「逃跑」这个词。

branches.en: A wandering life is flight slowed down into a habit.
branches.cn: 飘泊的生活是把逃跑放慢成一种习惯。

branches.en: Occasional verse was made to vanish, which is why it borrowed this word.
branches.cn: 应景诗本就注定消失，所以借用了这个词。

intro.en: Fugitive is a Latin adjective that became an English noun and adjective, with adverbs and abstract nouns built on it.
intro.cn: fugitive 是拉丁形容词，在英语中兼作名词与形容词，并由此构成副词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fugere, to flee, gives fuga, a flight, and fugitivus, fleeing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fugere（逃跑）给出 fuga（逃亡）与 fugitivus（逃跑的）。

items.example: Fugere is the verb at the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: fugere 是这个词族核心的动词。

items.example: Fuga names the act of running away.
items.exampleCN: fuga 指逃跑这一行为。

items.example: Fugitivus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: fugitivus 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Fugax adds the sense of rapid fading.
items.exampleCN: fugax 增添了迅速消逝的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ive marks the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 标示形容词。

items.example: English fugitive works as noun and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语 fugitive 兼作名词与形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词。

items.example: The adverb adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 副词在形容词后加 -ly。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成抽象名词。

items.example: The noun adds -ness to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词在形容词后加 -ness。
